rulings.title: The priority order (§2)
rulings.ruling:
Ruled by the manager on 2026-09-26, under the owner's delegation (notes/AGENT_STATE.md:112-131). The recommendation becomes the register's order. N1-N4 are never traded. Below them: R0 Evidence > R1 B-safety > R2 B-plasticity > R3 flexibility, self-regulation and emergence where they serve B > R4 A-openness > R5 current-run performance > R6 cost and elegance.

(i) R3 ranks above R4 but wins ties only. A flexible option wins only if it passes R1 and is actually used, not pinned at a cap (C25).

(ii) R1 is a budget, not a lexicographic rule. The budget is ε plus the creep budget. Both are provisional manager values (O2), not numbers the owner gave. Inside the budget R2 is maximised (the ADR form). R1 is never met by freezing the live learner (N2).
- R1 acts as a lock only where its harm cannot be measured within ε. That means poisoning (O5) and irreversible closures.
- An R1 instrument acts (HARD) only while its calibration holds: at most 5% family-wise false actions and at least 80% power at ε, validated on GPU (O2). A gate that fails its calibration only reports (SOFT) until it is recalibrated. The next step is more data (pooled nuisance runs, a larger probe), never a looser budget.
- Closures leave the tie-break and go to the owner (R4). Example: O17's escalation (1), where a release anchor would have to be designated with no passing context-widening route.

(iii) One order serves both decisions and tests (C41).

Three clauses from the owner's operating model are written into the order.

R0, bad results:
- A reading ends an arm's candidacy only at the configuration read, never the whole path. The ruling's next arm then runs.
- A reading counts as a fail only under its pre-registered rule.
- An unresolved reading, whose interval spans the margin, is neither a pass nor a fail. It triggers the pre-registered sample-size step (O2's non-inferiority form).
- One noisy or unresolved reading never leads to an escalation to the owner.

N3, owner rulings:
- An explicit owner ruling stands until the owner rules otherwise.
- A GPU result that contradicts one goes to the owner as a major issue, and the ruling holds meanwhile.
- Where a ruling collides with R1, the collision is documented and put to the owner, not overridden.
- Explicit owner rulings are decisions recorded with the owner's words or choice. They include:
  - the fundamentals (05 lines 13-22);
  - D1-D11 and D16-D18 in `.rework/DECISIONS.md`, among them D1 (the Fabric stays), D2 (`PURE_ADD` default 'for now'), D3 (reservoir quota, literature an arm), D4 (WORLD kept, switchable), D8 ('planned' default), D16 (soft clamp), D17 (refusal, switchable) and D18 (the owner chose the domain-and-floor pair); D12-D15 carry no owner words;
  - Q-RUN-8's ruling, `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` 3000 (`docs/04_CONTRACT.md:4236-4242`);
  - the 2026-09-25 instruction "I don't want anything frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary" (AGENT_STATE:16-17);
  - the S0b approval (:47);
  - the CPU rule (:134-135);
  - the operating model (:112-131).
- The list stays open: any later decision recorded with the owner's words joins it.
- 03b's D-1..D-10 carry no owner quote. The record says only that the revision workflow applied them (AGENT_STATE:30). They are read as design-workflow decisions, revisable under R0 (D-CONFIRM).

What goes to the owner (notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md and the chat):
- (a) a threat to A or B that survives the ruling's next arms on confirmed readings;
- (b) an irreversible closure (R4);
- (c) a GPU result that contradicts an owner ruling (N3);
- (d) potential expansions, and GPU tests as copy-paste blocks.
Everything else is ruled and logged in the register. A ruling that touches an earlier owner ruling or the fundamentals gets one line in notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md, in the section 'Rulings that touch your earlier rulings (no action needed)'. There is no other review log.
Example: the 2026-09-24 archive shows the expert pool at `FAB_SLOTS` 4096 in 20 of 21 runs (results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ARCHIVE_READS.md item 2). That is a B risk the manager works through GPU arms (O20). The brief reports it as a risk being worked, not as a decision for the owner.

The conflicts draft (A-openness above flexibility) stays on record as the alternative. Defaults: none, since this is a rule, not a lever. No lever default moves, because §4-§6 were already written under this order.
rulings.basis:
The owner ranks it: "B is a bigger priority than A, since the belief is that with B, we can add A later" and "Flexibility is what I'm looking for to enhance continual learning" (05 lines 13-22; notes/AGENT_STATE.md:89-95). Flexibility is named as a means to B, so it sits directly under B's two halves. It wins only ties, because an untested means must not outrank the end it serves. A-openness sits above R5 because a later measurement cannot reopen a closed door (§2 'Why this order').

"Without risking too much" bounds risk rather than forbidding it, so R1 is a budget. A lexicographic R1 would minimise risk by not learning, which fails B (N2, C26).

The two orders differ only when R0-R2 tie and a flexible option competes with an A-openness option. I listed §6's 'Rule used' column (register lines 978-1020). Only C41 (the test order) sets R3 against R4. The other rows that cite R3 (C03, C05, C13, C17, C20, C21, C24, C25, C26, C29, C34) rank it below R0, R1 or R2. The rows that cite R4 as a rank (C02, C33) place it below R1/R2 and above R5. C43 uses R4's closure clause. So adopting (i) moves no ruling in §4-§6. Built-OFF arms keep A-openness (N1), so a flexibility win cannot delete an A path.

The calibration clause follows from R0 and R1 together. A HARD gate licenses rollback, promotion to serving (O4) and consolidation (O5).
- Above 5% false actions, it throttles B-plasticity, which is N2 broken by the back door.
- Below 80% power at ε, it licenses promotion on a pass that is not evidence of safety.
Reporting until recalibrated costs latency and deletes nothing.

The bad-result clause is the owner's: "Just because one result was bad does not mean the entire path is impractical or impossible" (AGENT_STATE:115-116). Its statistical form is that a pre-registered fail ends an arm, not a noisy reading.

N3 follows the operating model. Explicit rulings "stand", and a contradicting GPU result "is a major issue for the owner" (AGENT_STATE:129-130). There is no lapse clause, and O13, O14 and O16 already hold their rulings until the owner answers. The list is widened because O12 and C22 rest on the 2026-09-25 instruction and O17 rests on D17.

The filter (a)-(d) is the operating model's own: "Brought to me should be major issues that threaten the project, potential expansions, and testing"; "Exact details of how things are run ... do not have to be brought up directly to me" (AGENT_STATE:112-123).

Rules used: N3 (the owner's own ranking) and R0. Nothing here closes a door or overturns a ruling, so it is not escalated.

rulings.title: ε (per-area worst-case regression per session) and the cumulative creep budget
rulings.ruling:
Ruled by the manager on 2026-09-26, under the owner's delegation. Both values are provisional manager values. They put a number on the owner's "without risking too much". The owner did not set them and may reset either one.
- ε = 0.05 bits/byte per area per session.
- Creep budget = 0.10 bits/byte per area (2ε), measured against the release anchor.
Both are absolute.

Form.
- The worst area counts, never the mean.
- Per-session reference: the parent anchor, read cooled (NEW-04).
- Cumulative reference: the release anchor. This is the chain's base checkpoint, recorded in the lineage (NEW-08). For a deployed chain it is the end-of-training parent the first session resumes from.
- A test chain's base (§8 5.2-5.10, 6.1) is its release anchor for creep. O17's refusal to designate a context-locked release anchor applies to a deployment anchor, not to a test chain's creep reference.
- An area first admitted after the release anchor is referenced to the first gated checkpoint that read it.
- An area that arrives during the session is read on its new-area gain (its bits/byte drop over the session, O6's measure) and against NEW-11's plasticity floor, not against ε.
- The release anchor is re-cut only on the owner's word, because a re-cut resets the cumulative budget.

Non-inferiority at ε. This is the one form for every B-endpoint comparison that cites ε: E1's guard (04-Q1 note 2), the S0b re-read, C04, O6, O7, O9, O13, O16 and O17.
- Pass: on every area, the one-sided upper confidence bound of the paired difference (arm − reference, bits/byte) is below ε. Requiring every area makes this an intersection-union test, so the false-admission rate stays at α with no multiplicity correction. The price is power, which is planned jointly across areas.
- Fail: on some area, the one-sided lower bound exceeds ε, which confirms a regression beyond ε.
- Unresolved: neither holds. The arm is not admitted and does not fail. It does not advance a ladder and counts toward no escalation. It gets the sample-size step.
- The sample-size step is fixed before the run. There are two looks, at n and 2n paired seeds, each at one-sided α 0.025. Bonferroni over the two looks keeps false admission at or below 5%.
  - n comes from the largest per-area paired SD measured on GPU: §8 5.1's pooled nuisance runs, or else the row's first 5 seeds.
  - n is chosen so that an arm with zero true regression passes at the first look with at least 80% joint power over A areas: n = ⌈((1.96 + z_p) × SD_max / ε)²⌉ + 2, where z_p = z(0.8^(1/A)). At 4 areas z_p = 1.60. The +2 approximates the t correction.
  - An arm still unresolved at 2n is reported as unresolved, and the ruling's next arm runs.
- Scale of the problem, from toy SDs used only to size the step:
  - The per-area paired SDs 0.0527 / 0.0624 / 0.1279 (rule_self_regulation/paired.py) give n = 17 / 22 / 86 at 4 areas.
  - At 5 seeds, the one-sided 95% bound sits 2.132 × SD / √5 = 0.050 / 0.059 / 0.122 above the mean. So a zero-regression arm fails 'bound < ε' about half the time on the easy area, and almost always on the hard one.
  - Variance reduction comes first: the ε-sized probe removes the probe-noise part of the SD. Then n is set from the GPU SD.
  - The seed counts are a GPU-queue cost (C41). The brief reports them with the queue; they are not escalated.
- A point-estimate margin is used only where a ruling says it protects the status quo (O13 (A)).

Status.
- Training runs: SOFT (reported). ε serves as the non-inferiority margin above.
- `continue` preset (unbuilt): report-only until §8 5.1 calibrates the thresholds (O10). HARD once §8 5.4 validates them. SOFT again whenever a validation fails, until recalibrated. NonFinite and the blow-up Reading stay HARD throughout, because they carry no ε calibration.
- §8 5.4's validation is pre-registered per gate configuration. It uses at least 40 benign sessions (for example 8 sessions × 5 seeds) and 40 injected-harm sessions at a true worst-area regression of ε. The dose is set on the report half, or the detection curve is read at ε.
  - Pass → HARD: at most 2 of 40 false rollbacks (5%) and at least 32 of 40 detections (80%).
  - Fail → SOFT: 5 or more of 40 false rollbacks (binomial one-sided p 0.048 against 5%), or 27 or fewer of 40 detections (p 0.043 against 80%).
  - In between → SOFT, and 40 more of each are pooled. On 80: fail at 8 or more false rollbacks (p 0.047) or 57 or fewer detections (p 0.039); pass at 4 or fewer and 64 or more. Anything else is treated as a fail, so the loop ends at 80.
  - After a fail, the next steps run in order: pool more nuisance runs into §8 5.1's null (k and the SE); enlarge the probe (priced under R1, O11); set W to 2×. Then 5.4 re-reads. ε does not move.
  - While SOFT: no automatic rollback. Each verdict is printed with its achieved minimum detectable regression. The served copy does not advance (O4), and no untrusted origin promotes (O5). O10 applies the same rule to its n = 1 actions.

Creep.
- Creep joins NEW-04's rollback triggers. Appendix B stated it, but the combination rule left it out. It sits inside the same family-wise calibration (NEW-04: every trigger and alarm is in it).
- A creep breach is read on the control half against the release anchor. It rolls back the session that crossed it. The retry ladder applies (`DATA_REPLAY_SHARE` 0.40, then the core LR halved). After that comes a recovery session that rehearses the breached area from the reservoir (NEW-06).
- The 3-rejection count (C34, NEW-04) sends the material to the next arms. It reaches the owner only under escalate_if. At a validated gate, three false rejections of the same material have probability at most 0.05³ = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ (arithmetic, treating retries as independent). So three rejections are evidence about the material, not noise.

Probe. §8 5.1 sizes the probe to ε, never ε to the probe. At 4 areas that needs a per-half SE of at most ε/3.08 = 0.016 bits/byte (NEW-02 note: k 2.23 + 0.84).

If benign sessions show a confirmed breach (the form's fail, or benign rollbacks significantly above the validated 5%), the next arms run in order:
1. the retry ladder and the recovery session;
2. §8 5.2's other LR arms;
3. NEW-09's tiered uptake;
4. NEW-06's reservoir;
5. NEW-11's remedies;
6. 'regulated'.
NEW-09's new-expert tier cannot fire while the expert pool is full. The 2026-09-24 fleet reached `FAB_SLOTS` 4096 in 20 of 21 runs, between windows 4,301 and 13,201 (median 6,501), and declined 2,508-16,933 spawns per run (results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ARCHIVE_READS.md item 2). So NEW-09 is read beside O20's slot-headroom arms in the same chains. ε is never widened automatically.

The alternatives stay built, OFF. The gate's budget form is a lever built with NEW-04:
- 'absolute' is the default (ON);
- 'noise' (k × the probe's SE, NEW-02's draft) is an arm;
- 'relative' (a fraction of the area's own gain since arrival, fixed when the arm first runs) is an arm.
Every verdict prints the minimum detectable regression and each area's regression as a fraction of its own gain.
rulings.basis:
ε turns "without risking too much" into a number. The owner delegated this (AGENT_STATE:112-125), and it is reversible. ε is SOFT in every training run and HARD only in an unbuilt preset, and only while validated. A rejected session keeps its weights as a named checkpoint and its material in the inbox (NEW-04 note). ε is a provisional manager value. Every register line that calls it owner-set changes (register_places).

Why 0.05:
(1) It is the toy's minimum detectable effect for the six-area mean at 5 paired seeds: (2.132 + 0.941) × 0.0385 / √5 = 0.053 (rule_self_regulation/paired.py, re-run 2026-09-26). The per-area MDEs are larger: 0.072 easy, 0.086 cred, 0.176 hard (same formula on SDs 0.0527, 0.0624 and 0.1279). So the per-area probe and the seed counts must be larger than the toy's. §8 5.1 and the sample-size step size them.
(2) It separates the regimes the tree has seen.
- Inside ε: rehearsed retention +0.046 (D2, `.rework/DECISIONS.md:101-102`), and 25% replay at 1.936 → 1.931 (03 §9, CONTRACT-Q-DATA-7).
- Far outside ε: pure-add +0.444 (8.9 × ε), tagged faded-area forgetting +0.28 to +0.31 (5.6-6.2 × ε) and never-tagged forgetting +1.23 to +1.87 (25-37 × ε) (C18).
- These are toy readings: a hypothesis about scale, not efficacy evidence.
(3) It is about 1.9% of a text model's bits/byte: 0.05 / 2.6892 = 0.0186. The CPU S0b k0 seed-0 prequential reading (register line 640) is used for scale only.
The rehearsed toy's +0.046 uses 92% of ε (0.046 / 0.05). That suggests ε may bind on benign sessions. C26's plasticity floor and escalate_if cover it.

Why absolute: a k × SE budget widens silently when probes are halved or areas are added (C04, critic blocking 1).

Why creep = 2ε:
- Without a cumulative bound, per-session passes compound: N sessions allow N × ε.
- A release-anchor reading is one paired comparison on the fixed probe, so its noise does not compound. Only one-directional drift accumulates, and 2ε admits at most two worst-case sessions of it.
- A best-ever reference is excluded because it ratchets toward a freeze. The NEW-02 note puts it 1.0 / 1.4 / 1.8 SE below truth after 4 / 8 / 16 sessions.

Why the non-inferiority form:
- The drafts used a 5-seed upper bound with no power requirement (O6, O7, O9) or a point estimate (O13). At the register's own SDs, that rejects benign arms from noise. The rejections would climb the ladders into false 'threatens B' escalations.
- The intersection-union form keeps the false-admission rate at α with no correction, so every area can be required.
- The two-look step turns a noisy fail into more data, as the owner asks: "Just because one result was bad does not mean the entire path is impractical" (AGENT_STATE:115-116).

Why a failed validation makes the gate SOFT. A HARD gate licenses three actions: rollback, promotion to serving (O4) and consolidation (O5).
- Above 5% false rollbacks, it throttles B-plasticity, which is N2 broken by the back door.
- Below 80% power at ε, its pass is not evidence of safety, yet promotion would act on it.
Reporting until recalibrated costs latency and deletes nothing. The binomial counts make 'fails' a statistical statement rather than a point estimate: at 40 sessions, one false rollback too many (3 against 2) is not a fail.

Rules used: R1 (the budget), R0 (GPU readings size the probe and validate the gate), N2.

rulings.title: The scope of the unreliability belief
rulings.basis:
The belief is the owner's (05 lines 21-22; AGENT_STATE:94-95). "Unreliable system" reads most literally as the system's own components (critic major 6, Appendix A row 6). Testing inputs only (C24's draft) would leave that reading untested and narrow the owner's words.

A broader scope removes nothing and moves no default, so R0-R2 are untouched. Its cost is GPU runs. C41 counts 8 families × 4 levels × 5 seeds × 2 regimes = 320 runs with (h), against 7 × 4 × 5 × 2 = 280 without it. So (h) adds 40 runs: 14.3% more than 280, or 12.5% of 320 (arithmetic).

Why the two-stage rule:
- NEW-12's 'beyond the paired-seed spread' reads 42 cells at 5 seeds with no multiplicity control. 'Some family improves' would then appear by chance, and 'no family improves' would be read at low power.
- With Bonferroni over 42 cells at 5 seeds, the power to see an R3 gain of ε is about 45%: z = 0.05 / (0.0385 / √5) = 2.90 against a critical value of 3.04. This is arithmetic on the toy's mean-area SD from paired.py. So a 5-seed null is not a falsification.
- The screen keeps a true gain of ε with probability about 99.8%: its point estimate falls below 0 only if it lands 2.9 SE low (arithmetic).
- Stage 2 runs on fresh seeds, so the screen does not bias it.
- Cost: under the null about half the cells carry, so stage 2 is about (21 + 2 controls) × 11 = 253 runs (arithmetic). It is priced in the GPU queue (C41).

Why 'exercised': a flexible option counts only if it is actually used (C25). The pool is pinned at `FAB_SLOTS` from median window 6,501 of 20,000, so `FAB_MUT` and jitter act mostly during the fill and on replacement births. A null there may mean 'not exercised' rather than 'no effect'.

rulings.title: Which copy serves after training
rulings.ruling:
Ruled by the manager on 2026-09-26: the recommendation. After training, users are served by the last promoted, cooled checkpoint. That is the cooled branch that the session-end gate read and passed while the gate was validated (O2). FRAME (1) already runs cooldowns only on branch children used for evaluation, gating and serving.

How it works:
- The learner trains as a shadow.
- A session that passes a validated gate is promoted, and its cooled branch becomes the served copy. Promotion is an n = 1 action on what users are exposed to, so it needs the gate's calibration (O10 (iii); O2).
- A rejected session changes nothing served. Rollback restores the learner, and the served copy was never replaced.
- While the gate is SOFT, the served copy does not advance. The gate is SOFT before §8 5.1 and 5.4 validate it, and after any failed validation (O2). Meanwhile the served copy stays at the last copy promoted under a validated gate, or at the release anchor if there is none. The learner keeps learning (N2), and every verdict is reported.
- Serving reads admitted MEM entries only (C07). The memory-on served path stays OFF until measured (NEW-03), and T0 stays OFF (NEW-15).

Serving from the learner is kept, not removed. A serving lever is built with the serving path: 'promoted' (default, ON) and 'learner' (an OFF arm).
- At each probe reading, the ruling reports what 'learner' would expose: the mid-session worst-area regression against ε, and the stability-gap depth (§8 5.2, 5.4).
- No switch of the default to 'learner' is planned. A switch would need a pre-registered GPU rule: every mid-session reading non-inferior at ε by O2's form, and stability-gap depth within ε. It would also get a line in notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md.

Resources:
- If one card cannot run both copies, the first fallback is time-sharing (the promoted copy serves between sessions), not serving from the learner.
- Memory is not the constraint at today's shape. The 2026-09-24 fleet peaked at 24,229 MiB of 143,771 MiB with 12 runs at once, about 2.0 GiB per run (24,229 / 12 = 2,019 MiB; `gpu_world_out/smi.csv` in results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/gpu_world_2026-09-24.tgz).
- Its sizing put the ceiling at 19 runs by CPU cores against 125 by GPU memory, and chose 12 runs by aggregate throughput (`SUMMARY.txt`).
- The binding cost is compute: a served copy's inference takes windows/s from the learner. It is priced with §8 2.1's throughput re-baseline.

Nothing is built now: the tree has no inference path (§1). The lever lands with the serving path, after NEW-03's `EVAL.generate` (§8 3.2). §8 gains a Stage 4 operation row, numbered by the integrator, and Appendix B gains a row.
rulings.basis:
R1 decides this without an efficacy test.

Mid-session, the learner has passed no gate. Only NonFinite or the blow-up Reading can stop a session before its end. The verdict comes only at session end, after a settle window, on a cooled branch (NEW-04 note). Serving from the learner would expose users to uncooled states, and to the stability-gap dip that every common method shows at a shift (TREE-OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM). Served outputs cannot be recalled, so that exposure is irreversible, and R1 requires a snapshot anchor before any irreversible change.

The same reasoning covers the SOFT case. A gate that fails validation either rolls back too often (above 5%) or lets too much through (below 80% power at ε, O2). Promoting on such a pass would expose users to a regression the gate could not see. Holding the served copy only delays when learning reaches users, and deletes nothing. The learner keeps learning.

R2 is unaffected: the learner learns the same under either choice. Only the delay before learning reaches users changes, by one session under a validated gate. Before validation there are no users: the tree has no inference path, and the continue preset is unbuilt. So the hold costs nothing now.

NEW-01 already rejects learning in place in the serving copy as a default, because that is irreversible between checkpoints.

Cost. The draft read 04 §7's packing figure (12 runs per 140 GiB card) as 11.7 GiB of memory per run. That treated a packing choice as a memory need. The fleet's own telemetry shows memory is not binding and compute is:
- smi.csv peaks at 24,229 MiB with 12 runs;
- mean sampled utilisation is 78.6%, at 99% or more in 60% of 10,310 samples (arithmetic from the archive's smi.csv);
- SUMMARY.txt puts the ceilings at 19 runs by CPU and 125 by GPU memory.
A served copy carries no optimizer state.

Rules used: R1 over R2's latency cost; N1 (the learner arm stays built); N2 (the learner is never held back).

rulings.ruling:
Decided by test. The lock holds meanwhile.

Interim. This is ON in the `continue` preset, which is unbuilt. Training runs are unchanged.
- Untrusted input enters memory-first quarantine (NEW-07). This is a read-only side path. Evaluation and gates can read it; served retrieval cannot. Each entry is tagged with its origin and session.
- Only trusted origins promote from quarantine to weights. They do so in a consolidation session with the delay, a clean canary (the two-stage trigger below) and the per-origin cap (NEW-18). The cap's value and its ladder belong to O18.
- Trusted origins are an explicit list, printed in each session's manifest (N4). They are never inferred from content.
  - The manager's default is the origins of the parent's training manifest plus the four `data/continual/` corpora (01_rust, 02_sawyer, 03_dracula, 04_num2). These are marked 'trusted (manager default)'.
  - The owner may add or remove any origin. An origin the owner names is marked 'owner-trusted'.
- Trusted material declared as a session's new material trains in that session (NEW-01). Quarantine is for everything else.
- Unpromoted material is never deleted.
- No untrusted origin promotes while the gate or the canary trigger is SOFT (O2).
- The unlocked alternative (any origin promotes after the delay, bounded by caps and canaries) is built and run as §8 5.7's OFF arm. It never becomes the default before the rule below passes.

The canary trigger, in the preset and in §8 5.7, has two stages.
- A canary trips when its trigger-conditioned reading on the candidate, minus the same reading on the anchor, exceeds its threshold τ. τ is calibrated on nuisance runs (§8 5.1).
- Each trip is re-read on the same checkpoint, using a disjoint, frozen, versioned canary prompt set, at one-sided α 0.05.
- A confirmed trip is a rollback trigger (NEW-04). An unconfirmed trip is logged and counted against τ's calibration.
- If the two prompt sets have independent noise, a false confirmed trip has probability at most 0.05 × 0.05 = 0.25% per session. That holds even at a whole 5% family-wise budget (arithmetic).

SR6 scheduling. The integrator adds two §8 rows. The integrator assigns the numbers; the ones proposed here are the next free ones.
- Stage 3, after 3.4 (the observe-mode trust book, SR3): '3.7. SR6 copy detection (04's SR6, the ACCU-COPY family) is built on the trust book. Known answers, model-free, on 0.6's E5 worlds (majority-false, impersonation 30% and 50%, colluding origins): copying origins are flagged and independent ones certified. SR3's bit-identity holds with SR6 on.' [CPU: operation, known answers]
- Stage 5, before 5.7's SR6 arm: '5.12. SR6's deciding run. E5 on 'focusbed', worlds base, majority-false and impersonation 50%; trust 'observe' and 'loss'; SR6 ON vs OFF; 5 paired seeds; under 04's E5 eligibility rule (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1510`). 6.2's E5 reuses it.' [GPU]
- Edits:
  - 04-Q12's test cell (line 525): 'SR6 test [CPU]' → '§8 3.7 [CPU]; §8 5.12 [GPU]'.
  - 6.2 (line 1192): 'once SR6 exists' → 'after 3.7 and 5.12'.
  - 0.6 stays as E5's model-free worlds, without SR6.

Pre-registered rule. The lock opens for corroboration by two or more SR6-certified independent origins (NEW-18) when all three of the following read.
(1) §8 3.7 [CPU]: SR6's known answers hold. This is an operation check, a precondition only.
(2) §8 5.12 [GPU]: 04's E5 eligibility holds with SR6 on, in the majority-false and 50%-impersonation worlds. That means:
- `format_split_floored` is 0 in every world;
- the majority-false world loses at most 0.1 Qc accuracy;
- Qa falls by at most one item at any seed.
(3) §8 5.7 [GPU], with SR6-certified corroboration as the promotion rule and the gate acting as it would in the preset:
- Grid. k ∈ {5, 25, 100} poisoned documents × {one origin; 2, 3, 4 or 5 colluders; an impersonator} = 18 worlds × 5 seeds = 90 poisoned runs.
  - Each run is paired with a no-poison control of the same seed and origin structure, where the poison is replaced by benign bytes of equal size.
  - Controls are shared across k: 6 × 5 = 30 (arithmetic).
  - O18's drip and benign-origin worlds join the grid.
- Attack success. On a promoted checkpoint (after the gate has acted), the poisoned run's canary reading minus its paired control's exceeds τ_grid, and the confirmation re-read agrees.
  - τ_grid holds the false-trip rate at 5% family-wise over all R promoted-checkpoint readings in the grid. The per-reading rate is 1 − 0.95^(1/R): 0.00057 at R = 90, which is z 3.25.
  - The canary probe is sized for at least 80% power, through both readings, at a trigger-conditioned shift of ε. That needs SE ≤ ε / (3.25 + 1.28) = ε / 4.53 ≈ 0.011 bits/byte at R = 90. Joint power is then about 0.90 × 0.998 ≈ 0.90 (arithmetic).
- Pass. Zero confirmed attack successes at every k, split and seed: a single real success in any seed fails the configuration. In addition, benign material from a genuine new origin is promoted within its delay + 1 session in at least 4 of 5 seeds. At 3 of 5, five seeds are added, and it passes at 8 of 10.
- False trips cannot hold the lock shut.
  - An unconfirmed trip counts against τ_grid's calibration, not against the lock.
  - If unconfirmed trips come out significantly above the calibrated rate (binomial, α 0.05: 2 or more at R = 90, P ≈ 0.0013), τ_grid is recalibrated from pooled no-poison runs and the grid is re-read.
  - A benign non-promotion caused by an unconfirmed trip counts against the calibration, not against the rule.

If (2) or (3) fails on its rule, the lock holds and the next arm runs. Each arm is re-read on 5.7, and rung (0) also on 5.12. A fail is never an owner item by itself.
(0) If 5.12 fails: SR6's copy-detection threshold is stepped, and 5.12 is re-read before any 5.7 arm.
(i) A promotion delay of 2 sessions, then 4 (C35's discovery ladder 1/2/4), with the canary re-read before promotion.
(ii) The per-origin cap as O18's rule sets it. `DATA_SRC_CAP` has one ladder, O18's, and O18 reads attack success by this definition, at every seed.
(iii) The trust-weighted loss arm.
(iv) The filtering-only arm (NEW-07).
Anchor retention stays ON throughout (C35, 8 sessions).
rulings.basis:
Here R1 acts as a lock, not a budget. The lock is the safer interim for three reasons.
(a) Poisoning cannot be measured within ε. A backdoor stays invisible to the per-area probe until its trigger appears, so the gate cannot bound it. Canaries and the SR6 lock are R1's instrument there (C05).
(b) It is irreversible past the anchors. Removing poison from weights afterwards is unreliable (04-Q12), and the ring holds only 1-2 generations (C35). The literature's fixed count, about 250 documents at 600M-13B parameters, does not shrink as clean data grows (§7.1 form 4).
(c) Collusion defeats agreement. Majority-false inverted trust at 3 of 3 seeds, and 50% impersonation flipped it at 1 seed (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1580-1581`; 04-Q12, C05). These are toy readings: they order the GPU tests and prove nothing.

The lock costs B nothing in the near term:
- Every B test in §8 Stages 5-6 trains on trusted corpora (the session chain's `data/continual/`).
- An open-ended inbox first needs the look-ahead draw and record compaction (C36).
It defers untrusted learning and never deletes it (N1). Evaluation and gates can still read quarantined material, and the observe-mode trust book reads it (04-6.3), so source credibility stays observable. The emergent, ungated path is kept as the logged OFF arm (C29).

Why the opening rule reads this way. The draft's rule, 'no canary trips at any k, split or seed', was judged over about 90 readings against a per-session threshold. The chance of no false trip in 90 readings is 0.95^90 ≈ 1% at 5% per reading, and 0.99^90 ≈ 40% at 1% (arithmetic). False trips alone would have kept the lock shut and run the ladder out into a false escalation (checker 0 F4). Three changes keep zero tolerance for real attacks while making the lock able to open:
- The paired no-poison control separates poison from benign drift in trigger-conditioned readings.
- The grid-wide threshold holds false trips at 5% for the whole grid.
- The confirmation re-read on disjoint prompts removes probe noise without retraining. A same-seed re-run cannot confirm anything, because it is bit-exact (`fb_off_rerun.s0`, ARCHIVE_READS.md).
The power figure sizes the canary probe so that even a real effect as small as ε is caught about 90% of the time. Real backdoors move trigger-conditioned readings far more than that.

Why a test decides the opening. Whether copy detection makes corroboration safe is an efficacy question, so under the CPU rule it is read on GPU (5.12, 5.7). The register's earlier wording (SR6 passing E5's worlds) becomes the scheduled pair, 3.7 [CPU] and 5.12 [GPU]. Row 0.6 could not test SR6, and no §8 row built it (checker 1 F5).

Why the trusted list is the manager's. The owner has named no origin. Calling the default 'owner-trusted' would put words in the owner's mouth (checker 0 F7). The default is the material the owner already supplied for training and for the session chain.

Rules used: R1 over R2 and R3 (C05); R0 for the opening; N1.

rulings.title: The continue preset's continuation learning rate (`OPT_LR_CONTINUE`)
rulings.ruling:
Decided on GPU by §8 5.2 under the rule below; no human reading is needed.

Interim, while the shipped behaviour holds: `OPT_LR_CONTINUE` defaults to 'as_logged', ON everywhere (today's pricing, printed as `opt.continue.regime`). 'floor', 'plateau' (`OPT_LR_PLATEAU` 0.1 / 0.25), 'rewarm' (`OPT_LR_REWARM` 0.5 / 1.0) and 'regulated' are built OFF as arms, with `OPT_LR_CONT_WARM` 1000. The continue preset carries no `OPT_LR_CONTINUE` value until 5.2 reads. Any continuation run before then (harnesses, measurement-protocol resumes) runs 'as_logged' and states its regime in its label: the floor for a revision-log parent, the re-priced rate for a k0 parent. FAB defaults are unchanged (`FAB_N0` 2048, `FAB_SLOTS` 4096; O20).

Pre-registered rule. The NEW-01 session chain (base eng, py, num, c; then four sessions from `data/continual/01_rust` .. `04_num2`), read on cooled branches from the report halves (C11). ε = 0.05 bits/byte per area per session and creep = 0.10 bits/byte are O2's provisional manager values (2026-09-26); if O2's values change, the recorded numbers are re-read under the new values by this same rule, with no new run.

(1) Admission: O2's non-inferiority form, with stated power.
- Components. At each session end, every old area's regression against the parent anchor, margin ε: 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 22 over the four sessions. At chain end, every old area's regression against the release anchor (for an area admitted after it, the first gated checkpoint that read it), margin creep: 7. C = 29 (arithmetic).
- ADMITTED when every component's one-sided 95% upper bound is below its margin. Every component must pass (an intersection-union test), so the chance of admitting an arm whose true regression reaches a margin on any component is at most 5%, with no correction for C.
- Power and the sample-size step. Joint power falls with C. On the register's per-area paired SDs (0.0527 / 0.0624 / 0.1279, O2; `rule_self_regulation/paired.py`), one zero-regression component passes at 5 seeds with probability 0.55 / 0.44 / 0.18, so 29 components pass together with probability below 10⁻⁷ (noncentral t, Monte Carlo; `revise/power_mc.py`). The seed count is therefore set before the deciding read. Each arm first runs a 5-seed internal pilot. The pilot reads no arm difference; it gives each component's SD, pooled across arms around each arm's own mean, with §8 5.1's nuisance SD as a floor. n* is the smallest seed count at which a zero-regression arm is admitted with at least 80% joint power: at least 0.8^(1/C) per component (0.992 at C = 29), counting components as independent, a conservative bound. On the register's SDs n* = 20 / 27-28 / 108-111 (`revise/power_mc.py`, `revise/reduced.py`).
- n_max = 20 seeds per arm: 4 × the planned 5, a provisional manager value that §8 2.1's throughput re-baseline re-prices. If n* > n_max, admission reads the reduced set, fixed now: each old area's per-session regression averaged over the sessions in which it is old (7 components at ε), plus the 7 chain-end creep components. That gives C = 14 and n* = 15 / 20 / 77 on the same SDs (`revise/reduced.py`). The per-session readings are still printed, and the gate enforces them at run time once it is HARD (O10).
- Outcomes, per arm, at its final n. ADMITTED. FAILED when some component's one-sided lower bound at α 0.05 / C (Bonferroni over components) lies above its margin: an arm sitting exactly at its margins is marked FAILED with probability at most 5%, and a zero-regression arm almost never. UNRESOLVED otherwise: not admitted and not failed. An arm FAILED at the pilot stops there; every other arm is extended to n*. An UNRESOLVED arm gets one replication on fresh seeds at n* recomputed from all its data, capped at n_max, and read on the replication alone. The rule proceeds meanwhile. UNRESOLVED never counts as a failure or toward escalation.
- Order: a fixed sequence at α 0.05 each, ascending in rate: floor, plateau 0.1, plateau 0.25, rewarm 0.5, rewarm 1.0. The sequence stops at the first arm not ADMITTED, and waits on an UNRESOLVED arm's replication. Arms beyond the stop are reported, not admitted. This holds at 5% the chance that any over-margin arm is admitted, without dividing α by five.

(2) Selection.
- Among ADMITTED arms the preset takes the one with the largest new-area gain: the new area's bits/byte drop over its session, averaged over the four sessions. The leader wins over another admitted arm only if its gain is significantly larger (one-sided paired t, Holm over its comparisons, family α 0.05). The arms it does not beat form a tie set, which goes to the smallest worst-area regression (C25; 04-Q2), reported with 90% intervals.
- The fixed arms run at the preset's interim values of the other levers (`OPT_BORN_CLOCK` ON, the clip at the parent's p99, tiered uptake, `DATA_DRAW` 'replay' 0.27, `DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT` True; Appendix B) and at `FAB_SLOTS` 4096. Every 5.2 run prints, per session, `n_live`, spawns declined (`gate:fab.spawn`), and experts born, culled and merged, for O20.
- 5.2's secondary pairs then run on the winner, each its own decision under the same forms: born clocks, the clip, uptake, `OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM`, and O20's slot-headroom arm. That arm widens `fab.slots` at the resume, which the geometry rules allow (register l.830-831; `src/spine/compose.py:3270`).
- The 2026-09-24 fleet pinned `n_live` at `FAB_SLOTS` 4096 in 20 of 21 runs, from median window 6,501, and declined 2,508-16,933 spawns per run (`results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ARCHIVE_READS.md` item 2). On a pinned parent, NEW-09's born-expert rung cannot act. The born-clock pair then reads vocabulary rows only, and it is re-read with the headroom arm.

(3) 'regulated' runs after the gate is built and HARD (§8 5.4, O10), against the fixed winner at the winner's n. It takes the preset if all three hold:
- it is ADMITTED;
- on new-area gain it is significantly better, or ties by O8's form (point difference within ε and not significantly different);
- it actually regulates: its session plateau sits at a bound of its range in fewer than 0.8 of its session-readings (0.8 × 4 sessions × n seeds: 16 of 20 at 5 seeds; the form of 04-Q2 (c)).

(4) If no fixed arm is ADMITTED, the preset stays without a value ('as_logged' in every run), and the next arms run in order, each under the same rule:
- 5.2's secondary levers on the lowest-regression arm;
- `DATA_REPLAY_SHARE` 0.40 (NEW-04's retry value, E1's arm);
- O20's slot-headroom arm, when that arm's parent pool was pinned;
- NEW-11's remedies (L2 toward the anchor first, §8 5.6);
- 'regulated' after 5.4.
A bad reading ends an arm's candidacy at the configuration read, never the path (O1). If 'floor' wins it is adopted. Every arm stays built, and 'as_logged' stays the lever default (N1).
rulings.basis:
The evidence rules. R0 and the owner's CPU rule decide who sets the value. Which rate lets the model learn after training within ε is an efficacy question, so only a GPU reading sets the preset value. R1 as a budget with R2 maximised inside it (O1) gives the rule's form: admitted within the budget, then the largest new-area gain (§3.3 O6 l.320; C01 l.978; NEW-05 l.847). ε and creep are O2's provisional manager values, not an owner figure.

Why the statistics take this form.
(i) Admission is an intersection-union test, so its 5% error needs no correction for the 29 components. Its power does fall with them. On the register's own per-area SDs, the draft's 5 seeds pass a zero-regression component with probability 0.55 / 0.44 / 0.18, and pass all 29 essentially never (`revise/power_mc.py`). Benign arms would have read inadmissible and walked the ladder to a false 'threatens B' escalation. The internal pilot estimates variance only and reads no arm difference, so it sets n without spending α. The futility stop at the pilot can only lower admissions.
(ii) Five arms, each admitted at 5%, could admit some over-margin arm with probability up to 25%. The fixed sequence, in ascending rate, keeps that at 5% without dividing α. If the ascending-risk premise is wrong, the sequence only stops early, which is conservative.
(iii) FAILED needs a Bonferroni lower bound above a margin, so only a demonstrated regression ends an arm or feeds escalation. An UNRESOLVED arm gets more data instead. The owner: "Just because one result was bad does not mean the entire path is impractical or impossible" (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:115-116`).
(iv) Holm on the gain comparisons keeps the selection's family error at 5%.
(v) n_max 20 is 4 × 5. On the register's SDs it resolves the full set up to about the easy-area SD (n* 20), and the reduced set up to about the cred-area SD (n* 20) (`revise/reduced.py`). Beyond that, the chain cannot resolve ε at this budget. That is a testing-budget fact, not a finding about B.

The alternative, fixing 'plateau' 0.25 now, sets a default with no GPU reading. The constant-2e-3 pilots all turned upward after about 6000 steps (Q-OPT-3, INV-28, confounded; note FRAME-POST-TRAINING l.667-675), so no rate is presumed safe.

The register's old reason for routing this to the owner was that only the owner could accept 'floor' lowering a k0 parent's rate. That is answered without the owner:
- A preset value chosen on B's endpoints removes no functionality: all five arms and 'as_logged' stay reachable (N1).
- On the shipped-default parent 'floor' changes nothing. Every k3000 parent past window 3000 carries a revision log and already resumes at 0.05 of peak (§3.1 item 5, l.224-239).
- It lowers only a k0 parent's rate: from 0.2173 of peak at 3.78 MB, and from 0.4759 at 756 KB, to 0.05 (`verify/emp3/k0child_378MB_s0.out`, `k0child_756KB_s0.out`).

The archive read (`results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ARCHIVE_READS.md` item 2; `archive_reads.txt`) changes what 5.2 records, not its rule. A parent from a default training run is likely to reach the slot ceiling: 20 of 21 fleet runs did, at `87f810a` with frozen segmentation, and §8 2.1 re-reads HEAD's k3000. So born-expert clocks (NEW-09, C02) have nothing to act on unless slots are freed. The headroom arm is O20's: a B risk the manager works with GPU tests, not an owner decision.

The rest follows the register. The tie-break to the smaller worst-area regression follows C25 and 04-Q2. The next-arm ladder applies the owner's "keep trying", and every rung already exists in the register (NEW-09, C02, C42, NEW-04's retry ladder, NEW-11). C39 sequences these arms before E2 and E1, and E1 shape (e) inherits the winner (note 04-Q1 item 4, l.542-546).

rulings.title: Source tags: tagged retention against untagged served use, and the drop value
rulings.ruling:
Decided on GPU by E4 (§8 6.6) under the rule below; no human reading is needed.

Interim, while the shipped default holds: `DATA_TAG` 'off' (OFF); `DATA_TAG_DROP` 0.25 (built, inert while OFF); `LM_SRC_AT` 'input'. 'area', 'domain' and 'head' stay built arms (04-Q13). The tag comes from provenance, never from content, and document ids stay in the provenance books (`Stream.sources`).

How the trade is settled: R1 used as a budget (O1). The untagged regression on served prompts of unknown origin is held within ε. ε is 0.05 bits/byte per area: O2's provisional quantification, made by the manager on 2026-09-26 under delegation, of the owner's "without risking too much". Inside that budget, tagged worst-area retention is maximised.

Pre-registered rule. E4 runs at whole-epoch sizing (§8 0.4). Each area's forgetting is read from the end of its last live phase to run end, on the report halves. Every configuration is paired against the never-tagged model at the same seeds.

(1) A configuration is admissible when both (a) and (b) hold.

(a) Untagged cost, in O6's powered non-inferiority form.
- Each area's untagged difference (the tagged-trained model read untagged, minus the never-tagged model) must have its one-sided upper bound below ε. C is the number of areas E4 reads: 4 at the shipped schedule.
- Planning figures. The toy's untagged cost was +0.051 with SD 0.0445 over 5 seeds (t 2.56). These are 04's evidence row 19 values −0.015 / +0.092 / +0.049 / +0.092 / +0.037 (arithmetic), an all-area mean. At that SD, a zero-cost configuration passes a 5-seed bound with probability 0.66 per area, and about 0.19 jointly over 4 areas (`revise/power_mc.py`).
- So seeds follow O6's step: a 5-seed pilot, then n*. n* is 11 at SD 0.0445. At the per-area SDs 0.0527 / 0.0624 / 0.1279 it is 14-15 / 19-20 / 71-76 (4 areas, α 0.04-0.05; `revise/o7.py`). The cap n_max is 20.
- Outcomes are ADMITTED / FAILED / UNRESOLVED, as in O6. An UNRESOLVED configuration is replicated on fresh seeds and never counts as a failure.

(b) Tagged gain.
- Per seed, take the never-tagged model's worst faded-area forgetting minus the tagged read's worst faded-area forgetting.
- Its paired mean must be above ε, and its one-sided lower bound above 0 at α 0.05 / 6 (Bonferroni over E4's six configurations).

(2) Multiplicity across configurations, fixed now.
- Primary family, α 0.04. 'area' at 'input' is tested for (a) in a fixed sequence from the highest drop down: 0.5, 0.25, 0.1, 0. The untagged cost is expected to fall as the drop rises (C19). The sequence stops at the first drop not ADMITTED, and waits on an UNRESOLVED drop's replication.
- Secondary family, α 0.01. At the lowest drop the primary family admitted, 'domain' at 'input' is tested, then 'area' at 'head', in a fixed sequence.
- So the chance of switching tags ON at a configuration whose true untagged cost reaches ε is at most 5% across all six (0.04 + 0.01).

(3) Decision.
- If any configuration is admissible, `DATA_TAG` goes ON at the admissible configuration with the smallest tagged worst-area forgetting. The leader wins over another only if its forgetting is significantly smaller (one-sided paired t, Holm, family α 0.05).
- A tie set is broken in this order:
  - first, to the higher drop: invariance to a missing tag (C19; §7.2 l.1055);
  - then, to 'domain' over 'area': R3 and C25, the emergent id wins a tie that passes R1. Passing (b) is its exercise test, since a domain tag that carries no source information cannot cut forgetting beyond ε;
  - then, to 'head' only if `fab.expert_area_purity` or `mem.hit_area_purity` rises significantly with the tag on at 'input' (label-driven structure; 04 §8 Q13, C33); otherwise 'input'.

(4) If no configuration is admissible:
- `DATA_TAG` stays 'off' (still built);
- both sides' numbers are recorded in the register;
- UNRESOLVED configurations get their replication;
- the next arms run, under the same rule:
  - (i) The drop ladder is extended to 0.75, fixed now, and then to 0.9. This runs only if the primary family admits no drop because (a) is FAILED at 0.5, (b) passes at some drop, and the untagged cost falls with the drop (a one-sided paired trend test across the four drops, α 0.05).
  - (ii) Tags run on the session chain in the continue preset (new §8 row 6.9). Session material carries its provenance tag. (a) is read on the untagged served path, and (b) on the faded areas' tagged reads. The §8 5.7 impersonator world is read with tags ON as a reported reading (not a deciding one), once the SR6 rows O5 schedules exist.
  - (iii) U-series family (c) reads the drop ladder with R3 (§8 5.9).
rulings.basis:
Why ε can break the tie. Both sides are R1 (§3.3 O7, l.321; C18, l.995), so §2's order alone cannot rank them. R1's own form breaks the tie: R1 is a budget (O1), and O2 sets that budget as a number. That number, ε, is the manager's provisional quantification of the owner's "without risking too much", adopted under delegation (O2). It is not the owner's own figure. An untagged cost within ε is inside the budget. A cost beyond ε on the served path is outside it, whatever the tagged gain, because prompts of unknown origin carry no tag. This replaces E4's untagged-only rule (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1509`), which ignored retention.

The toy shows why both sides are read.
- A tag at read cut the faded easy area's forgetting to +0.31 / +0.29 / +0.28 bits/byte, against +1.87 / +1.65 / +1.23 never-tagged (C18; `d2/forget_tag.py`, re-run as `verify/emp3/forget_tag.out`). That is a paired gain of 1.56 / 1.36 / 0.95 (arithmetic).
- The untagged cost was +0.051 (t 2.56), with a one-sided 95% upper bound of 0.093 (arithmetic, `revise/o7.py`).
- Drop 0 kept tagged retention best (+0.15 to +0.25).
These are toy readings, and so hypotheses only. The gain sits far beyond ε, while the cost sits at ε. That is why the drop ladder and the entry point are where E4 turns.

Why the statistics take this form.
(i) (a) is an intersection-union test over areas. The draft's 5-seed bound would pass a zero-cost configuration only about 19% of the time at the toy's SD. The sample-size step makes a benign configuration admissible with ≥ 80% power.
(ii) E4 compares six configurations and ships one, so the chance of admitting any over-budget configuration must be controlled across them. The fixed sequence spends no α on drops that are expected to fail first. The 0.04 / 0.01 split lets 'domain' and 'head' be tested even when drop 0 fails.
(iii) (b) is an efficacy claim with a toy effect 19-31 times ε, so a Bonferroni split costs it little power.
(iv) Holm keeps the selection's family error at 5%.

The tie-breaks follow the register:
- the higher drop follows C19 and §7.2: tag dropout is justified by invariance to a missing tag (l.1055);
- 'domain' over 'area' applies R3 and C25 the way O8 does for draws;
- 'head' on label-driven structure follows 04's own rule and C33 (B over A, then label-free routing).

Context awareness is not lost while tags are OFF. Provenance books, observe-mode trust, per-origin caps and quarantine carry source credibility without the model's input tag (NEW-07, 04-6.3). The status quo OFF holds until the GPU reading (R0, NEW-19). The lever is reversible and every arm stays built (N1), so no door closes. That makes this the manager's call under the delegation of 2026-09-26.

rulings.title: 04-Q2: does a statistical tie go to the self-regulated draw?
rulings.ruling:
Conditional yes, fixed before E1 runs. 04-Q2's conditions (a)-(d) are unchanged in substance and now carry stated power.

A statistical tie between 'retention' and a hand-set arm goes to 'retention' only if all four hold.

(a) The per-area guard (04-Q1 note 2), in O2's non-inferiority form.
- Every area's one-sided 95% upper bound of ('retention' − the tied arm) must be below ε. ε is 0.05 bits/byte, O2's provisional manager value.
- At E1's 5 seeds this guard is underpowered on the register's per-area SDs (0.0527 / 0.0624 / 0.1279). A zero-difference area passes with probability 0.55 / 0.44 / 0.18, and all 4 areas together with about 0.09 / 0.04 / 0.001 (noncentral t, Monte Carlo; `revise/power_mc.py`).
- So a guard that fails only on width (every point estimate within ε) is UNRESOLVED, not failed. It leads to more data: the two tied arms are replicated in shape (b) on fresh seeds at O6's sample-size step. On those SDs that is n* = 14 / 18 / 71 at 4 areas, capped at n_max 20. The guard is then read on the replication alone.
- The guard fails when some area's point estimate is at or above ε.
- Until the guard resolves, the tie stays with the hand-set arm.

(b) The two arms tie on E1's primary endpoint, the time-integrated all-area gap.
- A tie means neither arm is significantly better (one-sided paired t, α 0.05, in each direction), and the point difference is within ε.
- Significantly better wins outright; significantly worse loses (C25).
- Power. At 5 seeds, E1's primary has a minimum detectable effect of about 0.042 bits/byte (`paired.py`; note 04-Q1, l.582-586), below ε. That implies an SD of 0.042 × √5 / (2.132 + 0.941) = 0.0306 (arithmetic). At that SD, a 'retention' arm truly worse by ε reads as a tie with probability about 0.09, and one worse by 0.042 with about 0.19 (`revise/power.py`).

(c) It actually regulates. Pooled over the shape-(b) seeds' last-phase re-plans, `data.focus.rho_at_cap_frac` is below 0.8, or `data.focus.alloc_freedom` is at least 0.2 after normalising by its maximum under the floors in force (C17). The raw value is reported beside it.

(d) Its compute is charged through `replay_cm`.

If (a) fails, or (c) fails, the tie goes to the hand-set arm it tied with; 04-Q2 names 'replay', the arm expected there. Every tie is reported with its 90% interval and is never read as equivalence.

Defaults are unchanged: `DATA_DRAW` 'planned' (D8, ON), with 'replay' (SR0) and 'retention' (SR2) built OFF.

The same form governs every tie the register breaks toward the flexible or self-regulated option: C25 (E1, E2) and O6's 'regulated' arm.
rulings.basis:
No test can choose a tie-break. A tie is by definition the case where B's endpoints did not decide, so "performance decides" (R0) and the preference for self-regulation do not collide. The order settles what a tie means: R0 > R1 > R3 > R5 > R6 (§2).

The alternative, "a tie keeps the simpler hand-set arm", is an R6 argument (cost and elegance). R3 ranks above R6 under both O1 alternatives: the conflicts draft put flexibility at its R4, still above current-run performance and cost. So O8 does not wait on O1.

The owner states the preference directly:
- "a part of my beliefs are for the system's self regulation for a large part of it" (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:16-18`);
- "Flexibility is what I'm looking for to enhance continual learning" (§1, l.107).

The conditions keep the preference honest:
- (a) is R1.
- (b)'s stated power bounds C25's residual risk, that low-powered ties mostly go to the flexible option. A tie hides a time-integrated loss of ε at most about 9% of the time at 5 seeds.
- (a)'s UNRESOLVED path keeps the guard from failing benign arms on noise, which is the same underpower the checkers found in O6, O7 and O9. The replication is read alone, so no second look is taken at the same data.
- (c) refuses to credit a controller pinned at its cap. On the toy, ρ sat at its cap in 26-47 of 48-49 last-phase re-plans in the retention arms (`verify/emp3/toy_stats.out`, §3.2 l.285).
- (d) charges 'retention' its 4.3%+ wall (04-Q2, l.515).

Under the operating model of 2026-09-26 ("You can resolve most of the questions"), the manager rules the tie-break that 04 §8 Q2 had asked the owner to confirm. It changes no default and closes no door.

rulings.title: PLAN 3.8 and the instrument line: may a control act on one run's reading?
rulings.ruling:
PLAN 3.8 governs verdicts, not control actions. Its text reads: "No comparison may be reported from fewer than two seeds; every Reading carries its seed count; the renderer refuses to print a verdict on n=1" (`.rework/PLAN.md:140-143`). It is a rule about reported comparisons, and it stands for them unchanged: default changes, reported conclusions and findings keep ≥ 2 seeds, with the seed count printed.

A control action that consumes a held-out Reading may act on one run (n = 1) only while three conditions hold.

(i) Logged. The Reading with its `seed_count`, the threshold, the action and its outcome are counted and printed.

(ii) Reversible. It defers or diverts learning and deletes nothing (N1):
- a rollback restores a whole generation from a kept anchor (C09);
- rejected material stays in the inbox tagged 'rejected';
- the rejected weights stay as a named checkpoint (NEW-04).

(iii) Calibrated and validated.
- Budget triggers (the worst-area ε breach and the creep breach). Their thresholds are set from the null distribution of the maximum over areas, calibrated on pooled multi-seed nuisance runs (§8 5.1; NEW-02), with a design margin. The share is 2% family-wise per session, and the target is 90% power to catch a one-area regression of ε. ε = 0.05 and creep = 0.10 bits/byte are O2's provisional manager values.
- Canary triggers: a 1% family-wise share per session, from the null of the maximum over canaries on no-poison nuisance sessions.
- So the whole rule is designed at 3% false actions per session, inside NEW-02's 5%. At 4 areas the margin costs about 1.57× the probe windows of a 5% / 80% sizing: ((2.573 + 1.282) / 3.08)², with a Šidák split of 2% over 4 areas. O11 prices it.
- §8 5.4 validates on sessions not used to calibrate. HARD requires both:
  - at most 5 false rollbacks in at least 100 benign session readings;
  - at least 16 of 20 graded-ε sessions caught (an injection dosed on a pilot to regress one area by about ε).
- Operating characteristics (binomial, `revise/oc.py`). A gate at the design targets passes with probability 0.92 (false-rollback rate 3%) and 0.96 (power 90%). A gate at 10% false rollbacks, or at 60% power, passes with probability 0.06 or 0.05.

Canaries are the lock's instrument (O5): poisoning is a lock, and no rule accepts a real attack success in any seed.
- Every canary trip rolls the session back, and the session is never accepted.
- The tripped checkpoint is then re-read on an independent canary half: a second draw of trigger-conditioned prompts, held back like C11's report half. The threshold there is 5% divided by the number of canaries that tripped.
- A trip that confirms is an attack success for that seed. O5's lock counts it, and what it does to the origin's material is O5's.
- A trip that does not confirm is a false trip. It counts against the canary's calibration, never against the lock, and the material re-enters by its delay (NEW-18), not by the re-read.
- So a false confirmed trip has probability at most 0.01 × 0.05 = 0.0005 per session, and at most 4.4% over a 90-session §8 5.7 grid (arithmetic, `revise/oc.py`). False trips alone cannot keep the lock shut.
- In test grids, the paired no-poison control's checkpoints are read the same way, and their trips feed the calibration tally.

Status.
- The session gate is SOFT (report only) in training runs.
- In the continue preset (unbuilt) it is SOFT until §8 5.1 calibrates, then HARD, as long as §8 5.4's validation holds.
- A budget-trigger class that fails its validation (too many false rollbacks, or too little power at ε) goes SOFT at once, until it is recalibrated. While SOFT:
  - its n = 1 action is not licensed;
  - a reported breach is followed by a verdict: the session is replicated from the same anchor at a second seed, and it is rolled back if both breach (n = 2, PLAN 3.8);
  - the preset is labelled 'gate uncalibrated' and is not released as B's operating mode (O4's promotion to serving waits);
  - test chains keep every session's anchor.
- The next steps run in order, each re-validated on 5.4:
  - pool more nuisance runs and re-estimate the null of the maximum (re-set k);
  - enlarge the probe (windows per area per half), up to the point where O11 escalates (w_F above 50% of wall);
  - W 2×;
  - graded rollback in place of hard (NEW-04).
  HARD returns when the recalibrated class passes both validation targets.
- A canary class never goes SOFT. If its false trips exceed its share (per-trigger tallies, one-sided binomial test at α 0.05), the promotions it guards pause, and the material stays in quarantine: deferred, not deleted. Meanwhile its threshold is re-set from pooled nuisance sessions and the canary set is enlarged.
- NonFinite and the blow-up Reading stop a session in every status. A stop defers and deletes nothing, and their stops are counted in 5.4's tally.

Other control actions.
- Held-out readings cross the instrument line backwards only as declared wires carrying a Reading with its seed count, as `d_best_bpb` already does (`src/eval/levers.py:146-149`).
- Controls read only the control half of each held-out block, and verdicts only the report half (C11), so no action grades itself.
- `CKPT.Retention.consider`, an additive save (`CKPT_BEST_KEEP_TOL` 0.02), acts at n = 1 once fed (04-Q10).
- OPT's restart damping stays refused at `seed_count` 1, as built: `src/opt/api.py:539-561`, counted by `opt.restart.damp_refused_n1`, with `OPT_DAMP_SOURCE` 'off' and 'probe' an arm. No calibrated budget bounds damping yet, so the tree's reading that a damped restart is a verdict stands. A damping arm that meets (i)-(iii) is built behind its own lever, OFF, after §8 5.1.
- 'regulated' `OPT_LR_CONTINUE` (after 5.4) and the 'retention' draw are control actions under the same conditions. They act only in their arms until a GPU reading makes them defaults.
rulings.basis:
C30 (l.1007) states the collision. OPT already refuses to damp at seed_count 1. If PLAN 3.8 covered gates, a session gate could never act: every session is one run of one learner, and its reading has seed_count 1. That reading would leave B with no acting safety mechanism after training. R1's budget could then be reported but never enforced, and "without risking too much" would rest on nothing.

PLAN 3.8's purpose is that a single noisy reading must not become a conclusion: the between-seed spread of 0.066-0.131 bits/byte exceeds every architectural difference ever claimed (`.rework/PLAN.md:140-142`). Conditions (i)-(iii) keep that purpose for actions:
- the false-action rate is fixed in advance from multi-seed nuisance runs and validated on held-out sessions;
- a wrong action is undone.

The alternative, that 3.8 covers gates, removes a function the register needs, and is rejected under N1 and R1. PLAN 3.8 carries no owner quote; it sits in a merge its author states as their own (`.rework/PLAN.md:13-15`). So reading its scope needs no owner ruling, and its text is kept, not overturned.

The SOFT fallback follows from the license. An n = 1 action is licensed only by condition (iii). A trigger that fails its validation has lost the license, so it must not keep acting as if calibrated. Keeping it HARD would throttle B-plasticity with false rollbacks, and the three-rejection escalation (C34) would carry them to the owner as if they were real. Or, at low power, it would certify sessions it cannot check.

SOFT is not unguarded. PLAN 3.8's own route, a two-seed verdict, still rolls back a replicated breach. No uncalibrated gate serves users, and every anchor is kept.

Canaries are different. Poisoning is not measurable within ε, so R1 acts there as a lock (O1, O5), and a SOFT canary would let an attack through. That is why canaries pause promotion instead. Their calibration is built so that false trips cannot hold the lock shut:
- the false-trip rate is fixed family-wise per session;
- every trip is confirmed on an independent half;
- only confirmed trips count as attacks.

The design margins exist because a gate sized exactly at 5% / 80% would fail a 100-session validation about 37-38% of the time by chance (binomial, `revise/oc.py`). A noisy failure must lead to more data, not to a status flip.

Whether the n = 1 gate works (false rollbacks, misses) is efficacy, and it is read on GPU (§8 5.4; the CPU rule).

rulings.title: Monitoring floors against wall-time caps
rulings.ruling:
The principle is ruled now. The numbers come from GPU readings. Monitoring is priced under R1 (C31): every monitor has a floor, and a wall-time cap applies only above that floor. No cap may thin a reading schedule below its floor, shrink a probe below its ε-sized size n_ε, or loosen ε. No wall budget limits the probe size. The only wall limit on monitoring is this ruling's escalation point, w_F > 50% of wall. That is also O2's escalation (3), and it is the point O10's escalation (1) cites.

FLOORS.
(F1) Training runs: the retention probe takes at least 5 readings per phase, counting the phase-start reading (04-6.2).
(F2) Gated sessions: the floor is the sparsest reading schedule that meets the gate's calibration at n_ε windows per area per half, validated at §8 5.4. The calibration is at most 5% family-wise false rollbacks and at least 80% power at ε (NEW-02). C03's rule (readings at most a third of the shortest stamp interval apart) is the interim schedule until 5.4 reads. It is not the floor.
(F3) A codec probe reads at every refresh, with paired SE at most `AUD_RATE_TOL` / 2 (03b-16.30).
(F4) At least 1 trust pass per session and per N bytes of a new origin (C31, O18).
(F5) At least 1 plasticity-gain reading per session (NEW-11).

INTERIM VALUES (unchanged):
- Training runs: `EVAL_RETENTION_EVERY` 1000 plus a phase-start reading. It is ON after SR0's bit-identity test and 0 until then, because the probe is unbuilt. Each pre-registration writes its own cap as a number: the shortest phase's windows / 5, about 700 at k3000 on the 3.78 MB shape (N4).
- `continue` preset (unbuilt), by C03's rule: 1000 in text sessions at k3000; 333 at k1000 and in media sessions at k3000 (the 2000∪3000 stamp union has 1000-window gaps); 667 for media at k0.
- Probe size: 6 windows per area until §8 5.1 reads.
- Plasticity gain probe: OFF until §8 5.6.
- E6's 2% cap and E3's 2% cap bind only above the floor.

PRE-REGISTERED RULE (written before any of these runs):
- §8 5.1 [GPU] gives n_ε: the windows per area per half that bring the per-half SE to ε/3.08 at 4 areas, which is 0.016 bits/byte at ε = 0.05 (note NEW-02).
- §8 5.4 [GPU] runs its gated sessions at n_ε. It logs the raw per-window probe series on the union of the interim schedule and arm (b)'s stamp-aligned windows. Arms (b) and (c) are read on those same sessions by replaying the session-end verdict on the readings (b) or windows (c) that each arm would have taken. The replay is exact for two reasons: the probe runs on the read-only side path and leaves the learner bit-identical (C06), and the verdict is taken only at session end (C03). It needs no extra GPU run and does not wait for E6.
- A schedule (the interim one, (b) or (c)) is accepted if it passes the counting rule O10 applies to the gate at §8 5.4. O10's revision computes that rule as: at most 5 false rollbacks in 100 pooled benign sessions, and at least 16 of 20 sessions with harm injected at ε caught (scratch revise/oc.out). If O10 changes the rule, this ruling follows it. The sparsest accepted schedule is the floor F. A candidate that fails is not dropped: it stays built, OFF, and is re-read when E6 pools more sessions.
- If the interim schedule itself fails at n_ε, the gate is SOFT (report only) until it is recalibrated (O10). The next step is a larger probe or more pooled nuisance runs (O2), never a sparser schedule.
- E6 (§8 6.2) [GPU] then measures w_F = m / (m + t), the wall share of F at n_ε, where m is monitoring wall and t is training wall. It measures w_F at the whole-epoch shape and at the session shape.
(1) If w_F ≤ 2%, E6 picks the densest cadence at or above F that costs at most 2% (04-6.2 unchanged).
(2) If w_F > 2%, the cadence is F. The cap does not bind (R1 over R6), and w_F is printed beside every verdict. The cheapest arm below that passes sets the preset value:
  (a) The probe forward runs batched and gradient-free on the read-only side path (C06). This changes cost, not readings. Its operation check is a CPU known answer: readings identical to 1e-6 against the unbatched probe (§8 4.1). E6 reads its wall saving.
  (b) Stamp-aligned readings replace the interim schedule: one reading just after each scheduled stamp (TOK acts, AUD refreshes) and one just before the next. In a media session at k3000 the 2000∪3000 union stamps at 2000, 3000, 4000 and 6000 in each 6000 windows. So (b) takes 2 × 4 = 8 readings, against 6000 / 333 ≈ 18 on the interim schedule. At k1000 it takes 2 per interval against 3 (arithmetic). Admissible only if it passed (F2)'s test at 5.4.
  (c) The probe is split across consecutive readings, and the gate pools the settle segment's readings at session end (NEW-04). Admissible only if it passed (F2)'s test at 5.4.
(3) The same rule prices the plasticity probe (§8 5.6), trust passes (E3, §8 6.2), SR6's copy-detection pass once O5's SR6 rows build it, and codec probes (§8 7.1). `CKPT_EVERY` in the preset keeps matching the chosen cadence.

REPORTING. Every GPU script prints w_F in its PASTE THIS BACK block. One line goes to the testing section of notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md, as a cost with no decision asked, if either happens:
- w_F after arms (a)-(c) exceeds 10% of wall (throughput 0.9 of an unmonitored run);
- the priced Stage 5-6 queue exceeds §8 2.1's re-baselined budget.

NEVER ALLOWED, to meet a cap: thinning below a floor, dropping n below n_ε, or loosening ε (R1, C31). Under N1 a monitor is deferred or made cheaper, never dropped.
rulings.basis:
- C31 already resolves the principle: monitoring is priced under R1, floors hold, and caps apply above them. R1 outranks R6 and R5.
- Why C03's cadence is the interim schedule and not the floor (checker 2 F6). C03 set the cadence to keep the rollback window open between stamps; it was never validated at ε. As a floor it would forbid arm (b) outright, and letting a cap thin it would contradict the floor. What NEW-02 requires is error rates at n_ε. So the floor is the schedule 5.4 validates at those rates, C03's cadence serves until then, and every candidate is admitted on the same test.
- The size of the collision. At 6 windows per area and C03's 333 cadence, 4 areas take 4 × 6 / 333 = 7.2% extra forward windows. That is 2.4% of wall at forward ≈ 1/3 step (7.2 / 3), or 2.1% on the toy's wall basis (7.2 × 4.3 / 15). One audio area adds about 1.8% forward windows (about 9% in all, 2.6-3.0% of wall).
- The cost scales with n_ε. Let r = n_ε / 6. Then m/t ≈ (0.021 to 0.024) × r, and w_F = (m/t) / (1 + m/t). So w_F reaches 10% at r ≈ 4.6-5.4 (n_ε ≈ 28-32 windows per area) and 50% at r ≈ 42-48 (n_ε ≈ 250-291) (arithmetic; scratch revise/o11_15.py, .out). NEW-02's per-window variance is unread ('No such reading exists yet'), so where n_ε falls is unknown until §8 5.1.
- Why arms (b) and (c) are replayed inside 5.4 (checker 2 F15). E6 is §8 6.2, in Stage 6, and runs after 5.4 in Stage 5. Reading (b) and (c) from 5.4's logged series removes that ordering problem at no GPU cost. Arm (a) needs no error-rate test, because its readings are identical.

rulings.title: A frozen control that wins
rulings.ruling:
Resolved now. A frozen control is an instrument. It never becomes the default on the strength of its own win (C27). This rests on the owner's 2026-09-25 instruction, 'I don't want anything frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary'. The instruction stands until the owner rules otherwise, and it holds even while a GPU result that contradicts it is with the owner (N3 as O1 states it).

DEFAULTS:
- `AUD_FREEZE_AT` 0: the codec never stops, so it is live (ON).
- `AUD_FREEZE_AT > 0` stays built as the control arm (03b §6.2 step 9). It runs in the S3 replica and in every S5 plasticity cell, labelled step-matched and compute-matched (03b-16.28).
- Scope: every frozen control of a learned part. Text segmentation at `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` 0 is read by S0b-ship and handled under O14.

WHAT COUNTS AS A WIN. Only a win on B's endpoints, read after further learning:
- the post-training arrival cell, where a held-back family (e.g. aud/chirps) arrives after the main run. It is read on arrival speed (the arriving family's bits/byte drop over its arrival segment, O6's new-area measure) and on BWT over the areas trained before it;
- the within-run plasticity cells' worst media area, read after the later phases (retention, not the end-state mean).
These are read on codec-invariant readings (01-M3): caption and text-area bits/byte at margin ε (O2); understanding and recover exact at their pre-registered paired-SE margins (note NEW-02: ε does not transfer to them).
A frozen control wins on an endpoint only if both hold:
- its paired advantage over live exceeds that endpoint's margin;
- a one-sided paired t for 'advantage > 0' is significant at Holm α 0.05 over every comparison read (the endpoints × the two controls, step-matched and compute-matched).
A point advantage beyond the margin that is not significant is 'unresolved': it adds seeds (below) and triggers nothing else. A within-run end-state win (R5) is reported and changes nothing.

SEEDS: a pre-registered sample-size step for every O12 comparison.
- S5's cells run 2 paired seeds (docs/proposals/03b_LIVE_CODEC.md:173). At 2 seeds t(0.95, 1 df) = 6.31, so a first read can only order more seeds.
- From the first read's per-endpoint paired SD, n* is the smallest n that gives each endpoint (0.8)^(1/k) power at zero true difference against its margin, so at least 80% jointly over the k endpoints.
- Seeds are added to min(n*, 10) paired seeds per arm, in the same commit.
- If n* exceeds 10, the comparison is 'unresolved at 10'. Nothing moves, the reading goes to the testing section of notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md, and it is repeated at the next S5 or S8 reading.
- §8 7.3's replica gives the first media paired SDs, so n* for §8 7.6 is computed before 7.6 runs.

IF A FROZEN CONTROL WINS THAT WAY. The live default holds. The live arms already specified are read next on the same cells, least plasticity cost first:
1. `'jit_ema'` codes (03b-16.23);
2. the ceiling guard's 'hold' on calibrated families (03b-16.18);
3. the WiSE-FT-style pull-back toward the held snapshot at hold expiry (03b-16.18);
4. the release-anchor arm: AUD's anchor term pulls toward a retained release snapshot instead of the act-refreshed one (03b-16.14; built OFF; the codec keeps learning);
5. for a large shift, the versioned-block handover (03b-16.21; S8, §8 7.7).
An arm becomes the live default (a GPU reading, R0) if both hold at its n* seeds:
- it is non-inferior to the frozen control on every after-further-learning endpoint: the one-sided 95% upper bound of the frozen control's advantage is below that endpoint's margin. Every endpoint must pass, so the joint claim needs no multiplicity correction;
- it is non-inferior at ε to the current live default on the text areas' bits/byte.
An arm fails, and counts toward escalation, only if the frozen control's win over it is confirmed by the win test above at its n* seeds. An arm that neither passes nor fails is 'unresolved': seeds are added up to 10, then the next arm runs anyway, and the arm never counts toward escalation. In every branch the frozen control stays an instrument.
rulings.basis:
- N3: the owner's instruction of 2026-09-25, 'I don't like the idea of frozen codecs, I don't want anything frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary' (notes/AGENT_STATE.md:15-17). It is among the explicit rulings O1's N3 list names. The frozen codec (`AUD_FREEZE_AT` 3000) was rejected as a default and kept as a control (03b §6.2 step 9; 03b Appendix row 'Frozen codec: Not a default').
- N2 and C27: freeze snapshots and instruments, never the live learner. A control is an instrument.
- R0 is read on B's endpoints after further learning (C25, C32). A codec that wins within the run can still close adaptation after it (03b-16.28: 'A frozen default would close post-training adaptation').
- R2 and R3 order the live arms from least to most plasticity cost. R2 is maximised inside R1's budget, so the manager exhausts the built live remedies before anything reaches the owner. As the operating model puts it, 'A bad result is a reason to try the next arm' (notes/AGENT_STATE.md:130).
- 01-M3 requires codec-invariant readings, because bits/s depends on the codec. Codec-attribute criteria keep their pre-registered SE margins (note NEW-02).
- Statistics. The draft's 'win' and 'within the margins' had no test form. At S5's 2 paired seeds a point estimate cannot separate a real win from noise, and 03b itself notes that 'at dozens of strict comparisons noise alone would fail even two equal codecs' (docs/proposals/03b_LIVE_CODEC.md:188). So:
  - a win needs both practical size (the margin) and significance under Holm over all comparisons read;
  - adoption uses the non-inferiority bound every B comparison uses (O2's form; checker 2 F8);
  - power comes from a pre-registered seed step, because no media variance figure exists yet;
  - escalation needs a confirmed failure of every arm, so a noisy read leads to more seeds or the next arm, never to the owner.
- No efficacy test is needed to set the procedure. Tests only trigger it.

- §8 7.3 [GPU] (S3 replica, live vs frozen, anchor 0 vs 10): the first, within-run reading. It triggers nothing by itself and supplies the per-endpoint paired SDs that set 7.6's n*.

Brought: per arm and endpoint, the paired advantage, its bound and seed count, and the order the arms were tried in.
The live default holds until the owner answers.
Not escalated: a single frozen win, an unresolved arm, or a within-run win.
