rulings.ruling:
Decided by test. The owner's rulings hold throughout: `WORLD_ENABLED` stays ON in every branch until the owner rules otherwise (D4; Q-WORLD-10; N3 as O1 states it).

INTERIM DEFAULTS (unchanged):
- `WORLD_ENABLED` ON (D4; Q-WORLD-10, 'the owner keeps it as the plug-in point').
- `WORLD_FEEDBACK` OFF (the 2026-09-24 GPU rule).
- `world_proj` born zero; `WORLD_FEEDBACK=1` restores the wired arm exactly.

THE CONTRACT'S OPEN LIST, RULED (docs/04_CONTRACT.md:3545):
(i) The forecast magnitude bound is built as a lever before §8 6.5. Its name is set at build; provisionally `WORLD_FORECAST_BOUND`, a multiple of ‖h‖ per position, default 10.
  - It is inert and bit-identical while feedback is OFF.
  - It is ON at 10 × ‖h‖ in every feedback-on arm (provisional: the instability signature).
  - `lm.encode.extra_ratio_max` keeps reading the forecast before the bound. The bound counts the share of positions it clipped; that count is reported, not a trip.
(ii) WORLD's own objectives stay. `pop(z).detach()` into `world_proj` is not built while feedback is OFF; it is built OFF, as an arm, beside any feedback flip.
(iii) Aligning MEM's keys with h + forecast is an arm only once feedback is ON and `MEM.blend` lands. With feedback OFF, FAB, the readout and MEM all see h alone, so nothing is misaligned.

NEW LEVER, built before §8 6.5 (N1, N4): WORLD's input gradient (provisionally `WORLD_INPUT_GRAD`).
- Default 'attached', today's behaviour: WORLD's losses reach LM.embed through the undetached obs_emb.
- Arm 'detached': WORLD reads LM.embed's output through a stop-gradient. It keeps its objectives and keeps learning, but no longer shapes the LM.
- CPU known answers (operation, new §8 3.7):
  - at 'attached', bit-identical to today;
  - at 'detached', the gradient of WORLD's loss terms on every LM parameter (not only `emb.weight`) reads exactly 0, while WORLD's own tensors still move.

§8 6.5 runs 5 arms (fb_off, fb_on, skip, world_off, detached) × 5 paired seeds = 25 runs, against 20 before (+25%, arithmetic).
- All arms run in one post-SR0 commit (note WORLD 3), with `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` pinned (O14).
- FAB stays at its defaults. Slot headroom is O20's; n_live and declined spawns are reported per arm.
- Endpoint: per area, the time-integrated held-out gap on SR0's probe (report half). The end-state per area and both prequential endpoints (last half, full run) are reported beside it.

HOW EVERY COMPARISON IS READ. Per area a, paired by seed, D_a = arm − reference; positive means worse.
- 'Within ε': the one-sided 95% upper bound of D_a is below ε on every area. Every area must pass, so the joint claim needs no multiplicity correction (an intersection-union test).
- 'Cost detected': on some area, mean D_a > ε, and a one-sided paired t for D_a > 0 is significant at Holm α 0.05 over the 4 areas (0.0125 for the smallest p).
- Otherwise 'unresolved', and a pre-registered sample-size step applies:
  - from the 5 seeds' per-area paired SDs, n* is the smallest n with at least 80% joint power over the 4 areas (0.946 per area) to read 'within ε' at zero true difference;
  - the two arms in the comparison get seeds added to min(n*, 15), in the same commit, and the comparison is re-read;
  - unresolved at 15 changes nothing. It goes to the testing section of notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md, and the question passes to the media route (§8 7.7).

PRE-REGISTERED RULES.
(A) WORLD's cost. C = fb_off − world_off.
  - C within ε: no change.
  - C unresolved: the sample-size step; defaults unchanged meanwhile.
  - C cost detected: read C' = detached − world_off in the same way.
    - C' within ε: 'detached' becomes WORLD's default input gradient. WORLD stays ON for A, and 'attached' stays built as the arm. One line goes to the brief's 'Rulings that touch your earlier rulings (no action needed)'.
    - C' unresolved: the sample-size step; 'attached' holds.
    - C' cost detected: not escalated yet. Next, in order:
      (1) The extended no-leak known answer is re-run on the 6.5 commit. If it fails, the leak is a tree defect: it is fixed, and the WORLD arms re-run.
      (2) A replication: 5 fresh paired seeds of detached and world_off in the same commit, read the same way.
      Only a cost detected again in the replication, with the known answer passing, goes to the owner (escalate_if (i)).
(B) `WORLD_FEEDBACK` flips ON only if all three hold (note WORLD (4), amended):
  (a) fb_on beats fb_off on the time-integrated all-area gap (one-sided paired t, α 0.05);
  (b) fb_on − fb_off is 'within ε' on every area at n* seeds (the seed step applies only if (a) and (c) already pass);
  (c) no fb_on seed shows the instability signature: `latent_std` < 0.9, or the pre-bound `extra_ratio_max` > 10.
  Requiring all three keeps the chance of a wrong flip at or below 5%. If feedback stays OFF, the next try is the media route (S6 (b), §8 7.7; 01-M8), where WORLD's claimed value lies, not another text re-run. A failed flip is not escalated.
(C) The skip arm changes no default. It reads whether WORLD's objectives are still needed once the forecast is bounded.

  - Q-WORLD-10: 'WORLD stays enabled -- the owner keeps it as the plug-in point for video and audio' (docs/04_CONTRACT.md:3574).
  The register's earlier recommendation (WORLD OFF on a retention cost) would overturn them. The manager replaces it with a remedy that keeps WORLD ON and isolates B's cost.
- Why 'detached' targets the right path. With feedback OFF, WORLD's only designed path into the LM is its loss through the undetached obs_emb. That path carried 45% of `emb.weight`'s gradient at initialisation (0.005194 against 0.006371; src/world/api.py:150-153; a tree fact about the path, not an efficacy reading). - Why checker 1's loss-weight arms (WORLD_PREDICT_W, WORLD_COLLAPSE_W lowered) are not added. - (B)(c)'s zero tolerance is calibrated, not a lock set by noise. In the 2026-09-24 fleet (results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ANALYSIS.txt:8-23; ARCHIVE_READS.md item 4):

rulings.title: The retok interim default
rulings.ruling:
Resolved now: reaffirmed. `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` 3000 is the owner's Q-RUN-8 ruling. It stands until the owner rules otherwise, including while a GPU result that contradicts it is with the owner (N3 as O1 states it).

DEFAULTS:
- `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` 3000, ON (firing) in every default run until the retok fleet's ship rule reads (§8 2.1).
- The mid-epoch act (LOOP_ORDER stage X) stays built and fires at every value except 0.
- 1000 is an arm; 0 is the k0 control (no act).
- The `continue` preset runs at the same 3000 (Appendix B's preset cadences assume k3000).

GUARDS ON THE UNMEASURED RISK (C40):
(1) Every dependent experiment writes `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` into its pre-registration and label. The value is the one its commit ships (3000 today), unless the cadence is its own arm. A run that pairs with pre-S0b records pins 0, the only value those records are equivalent to (before S0b the lever moved only counters; Q-RUN-8). The 2026-09-24 fleet is such a record. It ran `87f810a` with segmentation frozen (ARCHIVE_READS.md; note WORLD 2), and each run minted 594 ids that never reached training (results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ANALYSIS.txt:8-28).
(2) The retok fleet keeps checkpoints (§8 1.5). Every GPU script the manager writes that runs a default cadence past window 3000 sets `CKPT_DIR` at script level. The tree default '' is unchanged.
(3) The shipped cadence stays provisional until E2's held-out re-read (§8 6.3; note retok fleet (3)), read as set out below.
(4) The fleet's growth-blackout secondary is split at the window where n_live first reaches `FAB_SLOTS`. C13's alarm, and its `FAB_COOLDOWN` 100 arm, read only the part before that window. After it, spawns are declined for lack of capacity whatever the acts do. In the 2026-09-24 fleet the pool filled in 20 of 21 runs by median window 6,501, with 2,508-16,933 declined spawns per run (ARCHIVE_READS.md item 2). §8 2.1 reports n_live per arm at HEAD's k3000, the re-read O20 needs. FAB defaults do not move here: slot headroom and churn are O20's GPU arms, a B risk the manager works and not an owner decision.

THE SHIP RULE stands as pre-registered (note S0b-ship).
- M = max over 3 paired seeds of |bpb(k0) − bpb(k0_nuis)|.
- A cadence c ∈ {3000, 1000} ships if bpb_c − bpb_0 ≤ M at every seed.
- Among those that ship, the lower mean wins.
A 1000 selection is within the owner's ruling, because it keeps stream rebuilding live. It is applied and noted in the brief's 'Rulings that touch your earlier rulings (no action needed)'.

ONE AMENDMENT, made before the fleet runs. It covers the two outcomes that would put the tree back at 0: the rule's 'if none ships, 0 ships', and note retok fleet (3)'s 'revert to 0'. Neither is applied, and 3000 keeps firing. Each goes first to more data and the next arms; only a confirmed result goes to the owner.

(a) None ships. The rule's own false-fail rate is why this needs confirmation. Assume k0_nuis perturbs a run by as much as a cadence change would by chance. Then, by simulation (scratch revise/o11_15.out):
- a harmless 3000 fails the rule about 30% of the time;
- 'none ships' comes out about 16% of the time with no harm at all;
- more seeds do not lower it (0.157 at 3 seeds, 0.165 at 6), because the rule compares a per-seed maximum with a maximum.
So the confirmation uses a different statistic.
  - Step 1, confirmation. The fleet auto-fills to 6 paired seeds: 3 more each of k0, k0_nuis, k3000 and k1000, 12 runs. Harm is confirmed for a cadence c if both hold:
    - the mean of d_c = bpb_c − bpb_0 exceeds M̄, the mean of |bpb(k0) − bpb(k0_nuis)| over the 6 seeds;
    - a one-sided paired t on d_c > 0 is significant at Holm α 0.05 over the two cadences (0.025 for the smaller p).
    At 6 seeds this falsely confirms a harmless cadence 1.3% of the time. It confirms a harm of 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 paired-difference SDs 46% / 81% / 97% of the time (scratch revise/o14_conf.out).
    If harm is not confirmed for 3000, 'none ships' is read as noise. 3000 keeps firing, provisional as before, and the reading goes to the testing section of notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md.
  - Step 2, next arms, if harm is confirmed for both cadences. The remedies the secondaries point to each run as k3000 + remedy against k0 at 6 paired seeds, read by the same test:
    - `FAB_COOLDOWN` 100, if guard (4)'s pre-pin blackout alarm trips (C13);
    - the SIG-width re-derive at a resume boundary (03b-16.33). Its trigger has already fired at HEAD's k3000, model-free: +8.8% bytes per token over the whole tail at the first act;
    - `OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM` {100, 400}, if the loss gap sits at the act windows (per-flush bytes and loss, secondaries (c)).
    DOM Levels are built before the first fleet in any case (C12). A remedy that clears harm (harm not confirmed) and beats plain k3000 (one-sided paired t, α 0.05) becomes its lever's default, provisional until E2's re-read like the cadence.
  - Escalation only if harm is confirmed for both cadences and for every remedy arm (escalate_if (i)).

(b) The held-out re-read fails. It is read per area on SR0's probe (report half), the shipped cadence against a k0 pair at E2's shape (6.3).
  - Pass (the provisional label comes off): the one-sided 95% upper bound of the regression is below ε on every area. Every area must pass, so no multiplicity correction is needed.
  - Confirmed failure: on some area the mean regression exceeds ε, and a one-sided paired t is significant at Holm α 0.05 over the areas.
  - Otherwise unresolved. E2's 3 seeds cannot pass any area at the toy's per-area SDs: the bound's half-width is 2.920 × SD / √3 = 0.089 / 0.105 / 0.216 at SDs of 0.0527 / 0.0624 / 0.1279, against ε = 0.05 (scratch revise/o11_15.out). So a pre-registered step applies:
    - from the first 3 seeds' per-area paired SDs, n* is the smallest n with at least 80% joint power over the areas at zero regression (14 / 18-19 / 71 seeds at those SDs for 4 areas; scratch revise/power.out);
    - the pair gets seeds added to min(n*, 15);
    - unresolved at 15: 3000 keeps firing with the provisional label, and the reading goes to the brief's testing section.
  - After a confirmed failure, the next arms come first: 1000 if it passed the ship rule, then the Step 2 remedies, each re-read the same way. Then a replication on fresh seeds. Escalation only if the failure is confirmed in every arm tried (escalate_if (ii)).

Shipping 0 would change only the training-run default. The act stays built for resume, AUD and continuation sessions (S0b-ship).

rulings.title: The wire budget at IMG or ROUTE design
rulings.ruling:
Resolved now. This is a contract ruling; no measurement decides it.

DEFAULTS:
- `WIRE_BUDGET` stays 25. 19 are spent (docs/03_WIRING.md:41), so 6 remain. AUD's two wires make 21 and VID's two make 23 (03-16.5), leaving 2.
- The ledger's budget check stays ON.

THE ROUTE WHEN A DESIGN NEEDS MORE WIRES. Raise `WIRE_BUDGET` in the same commit that adds the wires, by exactly the number the design's wiring plan declares. Each wire carries its written `why`. The same commit:
- re-renders docs/03_WIRING.md;
- passes `tools/sync_counts.py --check`, K13 (tests/test_contract.py) and the two-directional ownership tests (tests/test_ownership.py).
If any of these refuses, that is a build defect, fixed in that commit.

VISIBILITY. Every raise is listed in notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md beside the design that spends it (IMG, VID or a ROUTE package). That design reaches the owner as a potential expansion anyway. The raise itself asks for no decision.

The multi-source counting rule ('multi-source wires into one consumer field count once', 03 §16.5) is not adopted:
- A consumer that needs values from several sources gets one field and one wire per source, each counted.
- So VID's latent width reaches WORLD in its own field on its own wire, beside `WORLD.d_media_lat <- AUD.d`.

No wire is reserved. Wires 24-25 go to whichever design needs them first (IMG, VID, or ROUTE as a package), because a raise is always available. Wire scarcity is therefore no longer a reason for or against a design: 02-R6's 'revisit a package only if wires free' now reads 'on the paired depth arms'.

The CAP reporting wires may be deleted only after C28's equivalence known answer, and only as a move of their function. They are never deleted to fund the budget (N1).
rulings.basis:
- The ledger's own text names the route: 'raising it is one edit. Do that only in a commit that says why the coupling graph needs to be larger' (src/spine/wire.py:262-267). It also says 'WIRE_BUDGET IS A SPEED BUMP, NOT THE GUARANTEE': the load-bearing checks are the two-directional ownership tests (src/spine/wire.py:44-54). A raise keeps every check intact and is reversible.
- The ledger refuses two wires into one field as the silent-overwrite class: 'if the receiver needs both values it needs two fields' (src/spine/wire.py:250-259). Counting multi-source edges once would need a new ledger form, and it would make the number understate the graph the ledger exists to make visible. No function is gained, and nothing built is removed (N1).
- No owner ruling sets the budget. 03 §16 routed it to the owner ('Stay inside 25; no multi-source ruling yet', docs/proposals/03_AUDIO_VIDEO.md:818; 'unless the owner rules that multi-source wires into one consumer field count once (open question)', :389). The owner never ruled, and under the 2026-09-26 operating model the manager resolves it (notes/AGENT_STATE.md:112-131).
- The one earlier record on spending wires is in D17's implementation notes. An implementing agent was told to 'report rather than spend one' when five wires were unaffordable (.rework/DECISIONS.md:453-460). That instruction covered one implementation and carries no owner quote. A raise in its own commit, plus a line in the brief, keeps its intent, because the spend is reported.

rulings.title: The training-run DATA_DRAW default ('planned' per D8 vs 'replay' 0.27)
rulings.ruling:
Interim, unchanged: `DATA_DRAW='planned'` (D8) stays the training-run default, ON. 'replay' (`DATA_REPLAY_SHARE` 0.27, `DATA_REPLAY_NEWEST` 0.0) is built OFF at SR0 (§8 3.3), and 'retention' is built OFF at SR2. Pending fleets (the retok fleet, the WORLD re-run) pin 'planned'. The continue preset's 'replay' (O9, CONTRACT-Q-DATA-7) is a separate protocol value and this ruling leaves it alone; D2's measurement protocol pins its own draw.

The GPU pair (§8 5.3). Its rule is fixed now, before it runs.
- Shape.
  - 'replay' 0.27 against 'planned', both arms in one post-SR0 commit.
  - Whole-epoch sizing, so every phase is traversed (checked by §8 0.4).
  - `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` pinned and labelled.
  - Read on the report half of SR0's probe (C11).
  - A run that does not consume its whole epoch is invalid and is re-run. It is never read as a tie.
- ε = 0.05 bits/byte is O2's provisional manager value (2026-09-26), not an owner figure. If O2 changes it, the recorded runs are re-read under the new value by this same rule, with no new run.
- Seeds follow O6's sample-size step.
  - Five paired seeds run first, as an internal pilot. The pilot reads no arm difference. It gives each component's SD, pooled across arms around each arm's own mean, with §8 5.1's nuisance SD as a floor.
  - The deciding n per arm is the largest n* below, capped at n_max = 20 (O6's value).
- Primary: E1's endpoint (04-Q1 note 1).
  - The time-integrated all-area held-out gap, 'replay' − 'planned', tested by a one-sided paired t at α 0.05.
  - n* is the smallest n with at least 80% power at a true difference of ε.
  - E1's toy SD is 0.0306. It is implied by the 0.042 minimum detectable effect at 5 seeds (note 04-Q1, l.585): 0.042 × √5 / (2.132 + 0.941) = 0.0306.
  - At that SD, n* = 5, and 5 seeds give power 0.91 (noncentral t, Monte Carlo; `dec/revise/o16_dc/stats.py`). The pilot re-estimates the SD on GPU.
- Guard: 'replay' is not worse than 'planned' by ε, in O2's non-inferiority form.
  - Components: each of the 4 areas, on both its time-integrated gap and its end-state gap (C = 8).
  - A component passes when the one-sided 95% upper bound of the paired difference 'replay' − 'planned' is below ε.
  - All 8 components must pass. This is an intersection-union test, so its 5% error needs no correction for C.
  - n* is the smallest n with at least 80% joint power for a zero-difference arm, which needs 0.8^(1/8) = 0.973 per component.
  - On the register's per-area SDs of 0.0527 / 0.0624 / 0.1279 (O2), n* = 16 / 22 / 85. At 5 seeds, joint power would be only 0.008 / 0.001 / 10⁻⁶ (Monte Carlo).
  - If n* > 20, the guard reads a reduced set fixed now: the per-area time-integrated gap only (C = 4; n* = 14 / 18 / 71). The end-state gaps are printed beside it.
  - At n = 20, the full set resolves per-component SDs up to 0.060, and the reduced set up to 0.066 (normal approximation).
- Guard outcomes, per component, as in O6:
  - ADMITTED: the upper bound is below ε.
  - FAILED: the one-sided lower bound at α 0.05 / C lies above ε.
  - UNRESOLVED: otherwise.

Outcomes, at the final n:
(1) CONFIRM: the primary favours 'replay', and every guard component is ADMITTED.

(2) TIE: the primary is not significant, and the guard is ADMITTED.

(3) WORSE: the primary favours 'planned' (one-sided paired t at α 0.05, in the other direction), or some guard component is FAILED.

rulings.title: The position-table door (C43, NEW-13): no long-lived parent without a context-widening route, on either LM arm
rulings.ruling:
First, a correction of the premise, which both checkers verified. The learned absolute position table is not the transformer arm's alone.
- `_LM` builds `self.pos = nn.Embedding(geom.pos_max, w)` on both arms (`src/lm/api.py:144`).
- `encode` adds `model.pos.weight[:L]` before the arch branch (`:614`).
- So the default GRU (`LM_ARCH` 'gru', `LM_CTX` 128) also trains a 128-row learned table, which feeds the GRU at `:666`.
- `lm.ctx` is EXACT across a resume, as the 'positional table extent' (`src/spine/compose.py:3241`).
- `encode` refuses L > `d_pos_max` (`src/lm/api.py:599-611`).
C43's resolution ('Default GRU with LM_CTX 128') therefore does not keep the door open on its own.

Ruling, on both arms: no checkpoint is designated B's long-lived parent until its position scheme has a context-widening route whose readings pass.

Two roles are kept apart (checker B F18):
- The long-lived parent is a designation. It is a manifest flag (name fixed at build, for example `release.long_lived`), set only on a checkpoint meant to carry real post-training sessions: the one O4 serves from.
- O2's release anchor is a different role: the base checkpoint that a session chain's creep budget is measured against. Every test chain (§8 5.2-5.10, 6.1) has one. Those anchors are not designated. While their scheme has no passing route they carry the manifest label 'context-locked', and they are never refused. The designation refusal therefore needs no switch for testing.

Built, behind one LM position lever (name fixed at build):
- 'learned' (today's table): the default on both arms, ON. Every record and every pending fleet is unchanged.
- An extrapolating value per arm, OFF. On the transformer arm, relative or rotary. On the GRU arm, 'none': no table, since the recurrence carries order, so nothing is locked by construction.
- For 'learned', a row-append widening at a declared resume boundary, recorded under `ckpt.geometry`. This is NEW-13's route.
- The preset builder refuses, by name, to set the designation on a checkpoint whose scheme has no passing route. The refusal is switchable, following D17's precedent ("If it has a bad effect, we can turn off the refusal").
- `LM_ARCH` stays 'gru'. `lm.ctx` stays EXACT until a route passes (NEW-13).

Operation, on CPU (§8 3.6, amended). These checks decide nothing:
- the row-append widening's identity known answer: loss unchanged to 1e-6 on windows at the old ctx;
- the cadence-rescaling known answer;
- both extrapolating values build, run finite and resume exactly;
- the designation refusal fires by name, and its switch works.

Efficacy, on GPU: a new §8 row (5.12, if that number is free), run before any designation. Its rules are fixed now.
- ε = 0.05 bits/byte is O2's provisional manager value.
- Seeds follow O6's sample-size step: a 5-seed internal pilot that reads no arm difference, then n* for at least 80% joint power on the components, with n_max 20.

(A) The scheme pair, per arm: 'learned' against that arm's extrapolating value, at `LM_CTX` 128, whole-epoch sizing, paired seeds.
- Components: each area's time-integrated and end-state held-out gap (C = 8), in O2's non-inferiority form. A component passes when the one-sided 95% upper bound of (extrapolating − learned) is below ε.
- On the register's per-area SDs, n* = 16 / 22 / 85. If n* > 20, the reduced set is the per-area time-integrated gap only (C = 4; n* = 14 / 18 / 71).
- ADMITTED on every component: the extrapolating value becomes that arm's default. It removes the closure by construction and costs less than ε, and R4 weighs a closure before a reversible cost. The flip lands at one labelled commit, and pending fleets pin 'learned' (04-Q5's pin rule).
- FAILED on some component (the lower bound at α 0.05 / C lies above ε): 'learned' stays on that arm, and the arm's route must be (B).
- UNRESOLVED: one replication at a recomputed n*, capped at 20. If it is still UNRESOLVED, 'learned' stays (the status quo) and both routes stay open.

(B) NEW-13's widening reading, for 'learned'.
- A parent trained at ctx 128 is widened to 256 by row-append at a declared resume, then trained N more windows. It is compared with a parent trained at 256 from the start.
- Components: each area's long-range held-out bits/byte (C = 4), in the same form. On the register's SDs, n* = 14 / 18 / 71.
- ADMITTED: the route passes, and 'learned' checkpoints may be designated.
- FAILED: first 2N windows after the widening are tried, then the extrapolating value trained from the start for the long-lived parent. Widening is not abandoned.
- UNRESOLVED: replication, as in (A).

A scheme may be designated once (A) admits its extrapolating value (that value is its own route), or once (B) admits the widening (for 'learned').

notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md, 'Rulings that touch your earlier rulings (no action needed)': "Both LM arms, the default GRU included, carry a learned, context-locked position table. Under your 'nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary', no checkpoint is designated B's long-lived parent until a context-widening route passes on GPU. Test runs are unaffected."
rulings.basis:
R4 weighs an irreversible closure before any reversible cost, and N2 requires a fixed live quantity to name a route by which it changes between sessions.
- The designation rule keeps the door open, at the price of a build and a check at designation time.
- The alternative, accepting context-locked parents, closes the door for the parent that carries B's accumulated post-training learning. That learning cannot be moved to a new parent without retraining.
- A needs context headroom too: S5 reads "2-4 s clips that fit LM_CTX" (§8 7.6).

No efficacy test is needed to decide the policy. It orders builds and refuses a designation, and it changes no default.
- The tree facts come from `src/lm/api.py:144, :599-614, :666` and `src/spine/compose.py:3241`: both arms build and add the table, ctx is EXACT, and encode refuses an overflow.
- Rotary and relative schemes act inside attention, so the GRU arm's natural non-locking value is no table at all.

Keeping the designation separate from O2's release anchor (checker B F18) lets every test chain run without a switch. The refusal keys on the designation, which is the one act that would make the closure permanent.

The GPU rules use O2's non-inferiority form and O6's sample-size step (checker B F8; checker A F3's power point).
- At 5 seeds, a zero-difference scheme would pass all 8 components with probability 0.008 / 0.001 / 10⁻⁶ on the register's per-area SDs (Monte Carlo; `dec/revise/o16_dc/stats.py`). The door would stay shut from noise alone, which is the opposite of R4's intent.
- A FAILED reading moves to the next route; it never ends the attempt.
- Only FAILED readings on every route, at the point a designation is needed, go to the owner.

N1: 'learned' stays built and stays the default, so nothing is removed. N4: the refusal is a check, not a mode.

The owner's "nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary" (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:16-17`) is served: a ctx lock is a fixed live dimension, and it now has a route. The premise correction is recorded in notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md (the line is in the ruling). It is not an escalation, because no long-lived parent exists yet and the route is buildable.

The default scheme and the routes are decided on GPU by the new §8 row (5.12, if free): (A) the scheme pair per arm, and (B) NEW-13's ctx-widening reading. Seeds follow O6's step, and the row runs before any checkpoint is designated a long-lived parent.

rulings.title: Per-origin limits in the continue preset: DATA_SRC_CAP and the trust detection floor's N
rulings.ruling:
Interim.
- Training runs: `DATA_SRC_CAP` 0 (OFF). A training run counts as one session of curated corpora. The lever is built OFF at SR3 (04-Q12).
- Continue preset (unbuilt): the cap is ON at 25 documents' worth of bytes per unpromoted origin per session. The value is provisional (NEW-19). It applies to quarantine memory writes and to consolidation bytes (FRAME (7), NEW-18).
  - The preset builder writes the cap into the manifest at launch, as a number per origin (N4). The number is 25 × that origin's median document size in the session's declared material. For material without document boundaries, it is 25 × the owner corpus's median document size.
  - An origin's bytes above its cap stay in quarantine (deferred, not deleted: N1). They are offered again at the next session, under the same cap.
- The trust floor's N is resolved now, by construction. At least 1 trust pass runs per session and per N bytes of a new origin, with N equal to that origin's cap in bytes, so every capped admission gets a pass. With the cap OFF, the floor is 1 pass per session. Floors hold, and wall caps apply above them (C31).
- `DATA_SRC_CAP` has one ladder, this one. O5's rung (ii), 'a smaller per-origin cap', cites it (checker B F7).

The cap value is read in §8 5.7 [GPU], under a rule fixed now. Poisoning is a lock (O1 (ii), O5): no cap is kept if it lets a real attack succeed at any seed.

Arms.
- Cap OFF (0) and cap c, starting at c = 25.
- Every arm runs the full preset stack:
  - quarantine is ON;
  - the canary guard runs O10's calibrated rule: a 1% family-wise share per session, confirmation on the independent canary half at 5% / m, and a rollback on every trip;
  - promotion is open with delay 1 (O5's unlocked arm), so the cap and the canaries are the live guards. Before SR6, the preset's lock keeps unpromoted untrusted origins out of weights, and the cap then bounds only quarantine writes.
- Every poisoned world has a paired no-poison control. It uses the same seeds, sessions and benign material, with the trigger documents replaced by clean documents of the same origin and size.

Worlds.
- A single origin sending k ∈ {5, 25, 100} poisoned documents.
- k split across 2-5 colluding origins.
- An impersonator.
- A drip: one origin offering at the cap every session until the ~250-document count accrues (250 / 25 = 10 sessions).
- A benign new origin (`data/continual/01_rust`).
- A positive control: k = 250 from one origin at cap OFF, with canary rollback report-only, so that the attack reaches weights.
- A poisoned world runs ⌈k / c⌉ admission sessions, then the delay session and a consolidation session. At c = 25, the k = 25, k = 100 and drip worlds take 3 + 6 + 12 = 21 sessions per seed (arithmetic).

Attack success is measured on checkpoints that passed every guard, with a direct reading independent of the canaries.
- The reading is the trigger-conditioned target bits on a held-out prompt set, disjoint from both canary halves, against the paired control. It is taken at every accepted session checkpoint of the k = 25, k = 100 and drip worlds.
- A hit is one-sided significance at α 0.05 / m. Here m is the number of such readings for that cap value; at most 105 at 5 seeds (21 × 5). A hit is then re-read on a fresh prompt draw, on the same kept checkpoint, at α 0.05.
- A hit that re-confirms is an attack success. So a false success has probability at most 0.05 × 0.05 = 0.25% per cap value, family-wise (Bonferroni; arithmetic).
- Canary trips, rollbacks and their confirmations are reported as the guard at work. A trip that does not confirm, and every trip in a paired control, is a false trip. It goes to O10's calibration tally, never to the attack count.
- False trips therefore cannot fail a cap. They cost benign sessions, which the benign criterion reads.
- The same zero-tolerance count, with canaries as the instrument, holds a false success to at most 0.01 × 0.05 × 0.05 = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ per session: 0.26% over 105 sessions and 1.0% over 420 (`dec/revise/o16_dc/stats.py`). That count is used where O5 reads canaries alone.

Instrument check.
- At every seed, the positive control must show a direct-reading hit at the same α 0.05 / m and a confirmed canary trip.
- If a seed fails that check, the grid is not read, neither pass nor fail.
  - If the direct reading shows no implant, the positive control's k doubles (500, then 1000), and the ladder worlds are re-scaled to the implanting count.
  - If the canaries missed an implant, the canary set is enlarged and recalibrated (O10).
- The benign criterion is used for the ladder only while the canary class passes its own false-trip check, O10's one-sided binomial test at α 0.05. Otherwise the canaries are recalibrated first.

Benign delay.
- The benign origin's session gain, its held-out bits/byte drop, is compared under cap c and under cap OFF, session by session, in O2's non-inferiority form at ε. ε = 0.05 bits/byte is O2's provisional manager value.
- Delay ≤ 1 means ADMITTED at the first consolidation session after the promotion delay.
- Seeds follow O6's sample-size step: a 5-seed pilot, then n* for at least 80% power. On the register's per-area SDs, n* = 9 / 12 / 42; n_max 20.
- FAILED means the lower bound at α 0.05 lies above ε. UNRESOLVED gets one replication and never moves the ladder.

The rule.
(1) Keep c, and drop the provisional label, only if there are zero attack successes at every seed in the k = 25, k = 100 and drip worlds, and the benign reading is ADMITTED.
(2) Zero successes but benign FAILED: double c (25 → 50) and re-run the benign, k = 100 and drip worlds. Repeat, keeping the largest c that has zero successes.
(3) Any attack success at c: halve c (25 → 12, rounded down) and re-run. Repeat while the benign reading is not FAILED, down to 1 document.
(4) If the drip world alone fails at every c whose benign reading is not FAILED, build a lineage-cumulative per-origin ceiling as an arm and re-run before concluding. NEW-08's lineage already records admitted bytes per origin. The reason: under N1 a per-session cap spreads a dose over sessions; it does not remove it.

Reported, not setting c.
- k = 5 sits below the cap by construction and reads quarantine and canaries. A success there is a finding against O5's unlocked promotion, and the lock stays.
- Colluders: per-origin caps cannot bound k split over 5 origins (5 × 25 = 125 ≥ 100, arithmetic).
- The impersonator.
- A success in the colluder or impersonator worlds is a finding against O5's promotion rule. Those worlds are re-read under SR6-certified corroboration.

SR6 is scheduled (checker B F5). The integrator adds these rows:
- New §8 4.14 [CPU: operation only]: SR6 copy detection (04's SR6, the ACCU-COPY family), built behind its own lever, OFF. It must give its known answers on E5's majority-false and 50%-impersonation worlds, model-free. It must be bit-identical when off, and its counters must fire.
- 4.14's deciding GPU runs:
  - §8 5.7 gains an SR6-certified corroboration arm. It re-reads O18's colluder and impersonator worlds under the same attack-success rule.
  - §8 6.2's E5 'once SR6 exists' becomes 'after 4.14'.
- The Stage 5 mapping names both runs as 4.14's deciding runs.
- If O5's revision numbers these rows differently, O18 cites O5's numbers.
rulings.basis:
R1 over R3. Untrusted input is attributed and gated, and poisoning must be prevented rather than undone: "removing poison from weights afterwards is unreliable, so guards must be preventive" (04-Q12, l.525).
- Poisoning is count-based: about 250 documents, regardless of clean volume (04-Q12; the literature digest). So the cap is counted in documents, and 25 is a tenth of that count (arithmetic).
- NEW-07's ladder {5, 25, 100} brackets it: below, at, and 4× above (arithmetic).
- The ON interim in the unbuilt preset has a safety reason (R1). The training-run value stays the shipped OFF.
- C29: the emergent path stays as an arm (cap 0).
- N4: the preset builder writes the per-origin number at launch; it is never computed at run time.
- N = cap ties the monitoring floor to the admission unit (C31: monitoring is priced under R1). That is a structural choice no test changes.
- Which value trades learning speed against exposure is an efficacy question, so it reads on GPU (the CPU rule). E5's model-free worlds (§8 0.6) and 4.7's 'caps bind at their byte count' are operation only.

Why the rule changed (checker A F5, A F4, B F7).
- The draft kept a cap when attack success stayed within threshold at "4 or more of 5 seeds". That count comes from 04-Q1 note 5, which is a draw-share eligibility count. It accepted one poisoning success in five, which contradicts poisoning being a lock (O1 (ii), O5).
- Zero tolerance needs an attack measure whose false positives cannot fail a cap. It gets one:
  - Bonferroni control over the grid's readings, plus a re-read on a fresh draw, holds a false success at or below 0.25% per cap value.

rulings.title: Q-CAP-2, answered by the fleet archive: the expert pool does not settle at 1844, it fills FAB_SLOTS 4096; slot headroom and churn after training go to GPU arms
rulings.ruling:
The n_live read in §8 0.2 is done.

The 2026-09-24 archive was read by the manager on 2026-09-26: commit 047358c; `results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ARCHIVE_READS.md` item 2; `archive_reads.txt`.

Q-CAP-2 asked whether the population settles at 1844 from 2048. It does not:
- It passes the setpoint within a few hundred windows. fb_off.s0 already had 2,064 experts at window 301.
- It reaches the `FAB_SLOTS` hard ceiling of 4,096 in 20 of 21 logs, which is 19 of 20 distinct runs (fb_off_rerun.s0 is bit-identical to fb_off.s0).
- It first reaches the ceiling between windows 4,301 and 13,201: median 6,501 over the 20 logs, or 6,401 over the 19 distinct runs.
- It then stays there.
- The one exception is skip.s1, the unstable capacity-control arm, which ends at 3,927.

Measured further here from the same logs (`dec/revise/o16_dc/churn.py`, `refill.py`, with `.out`):
- Time at the ceiling.
  - After the pool first fills, it sits at the ceiling for 87.9-95.8% of the remaining windows (median 94.1%). That is 6,435-14,696 windows per run.
- Churn.
  - A manage pass runs every 500 windows.
  - Each pass frees a median of 27 slots (range 6-61), read one window after the pass, over 460 passes.
  - Spawning retakes the freed slots within 100 windows in 445 of 460 passes (96.7%).
- Where births come from.
  - Spawn-by-specification makes 99.5-99.9% of all births (`fab.spawned` / `fab.births` per run).
  - That door is bound only by the hard ceiling, never by CAP's soft cap (`src/fabric/api.py:2432-2444`).
- A correction to the archive note's wording.
  - `fab.spawn_declined` (2,508-16,933 per run) counts spawn tests that ran while a slot was free and found the query not novel enough. It does not count spawns refused by a full pool.
  - At a full pool the test does not run: `src/fabric/api.py:2079-2085` returns None, and `:2484-2488` counts a decline only when a gap was measured. skip.s1 declined 16,933 without ever filling.
  - Time at the ceiling is therefore 20,000 − `fab.spawned` − `fab.spawn_declined` at `OPT_BATCH_WINDOWS` 1, which is the figure above.

The fleet ran commit 87f810a (`SUMMARY.txt`), not d97779d; only `src/world/levers.py` differs between the two. Its segmentation was frozen, and the run read about 3.8 MB of the 20 MB stream, in phase 1 (eng + py) only. So the pool filled on a stationary two-area mixture.

What this means for Q-CAP-2. It is resolved by measurement, as a manager ruling (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:140`).
- Reading (a), `FAB_N0` ≤ 1844 so the population grows into its pressure band, assumes a settling that does not happen. A population founded at 1,844 would also fill the ceiling by spawning. The `FAB_N0` 1844-vs-2048 pair that the draft planned for P4 is withdrawn: the question it was meant to answer has been answered.
- Reading (b), the below-population clause compared against a settled population, rests on the same refuted premise. It is not built.
- Reading (c) holds at defaults: `CAP_TARGETS` stays 'off', and both startup-refusal clauses are unchanged.
- Clause (2)'s text ("The cull holds the population at about {settles}", `src/capacity/api.py:1640-1650`) and the `pressure` lever's help text (`src/fabric/levers.py:299-302, :327-329`) describe a behaviour the fleet refutes at the defaults. They are corrected as a low fix alongside §8 1.6. The fix is text only: logic and defaults are unchanged, and runs are otherwise bit-identical.
- A soft expert cap can bind only if spawn births honour it. That spawn-door ceiling is built at P4 with `CAP.observe`, behind its own lever, OFF. It is also arm R below. CAP's vocab arm still goes first (03b-0b4-CAP).

The B risk, and what the manager does about it.
- A parent trained at the defaults arrives after training with no free expert slot.
- A new area then gains experts only through churn: about 27 slots per 500 windows, which the next spawns take. This includes a new modality under "add A later".
- In the continue preset, C37's deferral of faded-area culls and merges lowers that churn further. NEW-09's born-expert rung cannot act at all (O6).
- Whether this costs B is an efficacy question, so GPU arms decide it. It is not an owner decision. The owner already has it in notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md as a risk being worked.

Defaults are unchanged meanwhile.
- Training runs keep `FAB_N0` 2048, `FAB_SLOTS` 4096, `FAB_PRESSURE` 0.45, `FAB_CULL_FRAC` 0.02, `FAB_SPAWN_MULT` 2.0 and `CAP_TARGETS` 'off'.
- The continue preset keeps the parent's slots until arm W below is adopted.

The arms run in this order. Their rules are fixed now, before the runs they govern. Every run prints, per session:
- `n_live`;
- windows at the ceiling;
- slots freed per pass;
- births, and births whose most-served area is the new area;
- C37's deferred culls and merges.

Arm P (control): the parent's slots are left unchanged at the resume, so the pool stays pinned.

Arm W (headroom top-up; no build needed).
- At each resume, `fab.slots` is widened to max(slots, n_live + H), with H = 2048. H is the founding run's free count (4096 − 2048). From a pinned parent this gives 6,144.
- `fab.slots` and `fab.cap` may widen across a resume (MAY_WIDEN, `src/spine/compose.py:3270, :3283`). WORLD's population is separate (`WORLD_NMAX`).
- Operation check: NEW-14 (iii) in §8 4.11 [CPU].
- Cost of one top-up:
  - 2 × 2048 × 128 × 8 = 4,194,304 floats, which is 16.8 MB in fp32 and about 67 MB with the gradient and Adam moments;
  - the card has 143,771 MiB, and the fleet peaked at 24,229 MiB for 12 runs (`smi.csv`);
  - the routing wall time is reported.
- If W pins again inside its first session at 3 or more of the 5 pilot seeds, the deciding read uses H = 4096.
- W is read in three places:
  - §8 5.6: NEW-11's plasticity gain on the 8-session chain, as a remedy arm;
  - §8 5.2: the secondary pair on the winning LR arm, with born-group clocks, which re-reads NEW-09's rung;
  - §8 6.1: owner scale, from §8 2.1's kept checkpoints.

Arm R (training-time reserve; built at P4, shared with CAP's expert arm). Spawn births are bound by a ceiling below `FAB_SLOTS`, for example 3,072 (0.75 × 4096), which leaves 1,024 slots free at the end of training.

Arm C (training-time churn; no build needed): `FAB_CULL_FRAC` 0.05 and `FAB_SPAWN_MULT` 3.0.

R and C change training runs. So each one trains a parent at §8 2.1's shape, and that parent is then continued as in §8 6.1. They run in the next owner training fleet after W has read, beside §8 6.3's training-run arms, or first if W is not adopted.

Decision rules.
- ε = 0.05 and creep = 0.10 bits/byte are O2's provisional manager values.
- Seeds follow O6's sample-size step:
  - a 5-seed internal pilot that reads no arm difference;
  - then n* from its SDs, with n_max 20;
  - outcomes on the old-area components are ADMITTED, FAILED or UNRESOLVED. The components are O6's: every old area at every session end against ε, and at the chain end against creep. If n* > 20, the reduced per-area-mean set is used instead.
- W is adopted into the continue preset only if both of these hold (the `FAB_SLOTS` lever default stays 4096 either way):
  - W is ADMITTED on every old-area component;
  - W's new-area gain (O6's measure; in §8 5.6, also NEW-11's plasticity gain) exceeds P's, by a one-sided paired t at α 0.05, with Holm correction if both H values are read. n* for this comparison gives at least 80% power at a true difference of ε: 9 / 12 / 42 seeds on the register's per-area SDs of 0.0527 / 0.0624 / 0.1279. If n* > 20, the comparison uses the gain averaged over the chain's sessions.
- If W is ADMITTED but its gain is not significantly larger:
  - nothing changes, and W stays an arm;
  - the result is reported with 90% intervals, never as equivalence (C25);
  - W is re-read at owner scale in §8 6.1.
- If W is FAILED on some old-area component, W is not adopted, and the next arms run in order:
  - W with born-group clocks ON for new experts (the §8 5.2 pair);
  - W with H = 1024;
  - then R and C.
- R or C becomes a training-run default only if both hold; otherwise it stays an arm:
  - its parent is ADMITTED against the default parent on every area at ε (O2's form, O6's step);
  - its continuation's new-area gain exceeds P's (one-sided paired t, Holm over R and C).
- UNRESOLVED anywhere means one replication at a recomputed n*, capped at 20. It never moves the ladder forward and never counts toward escalation.

§8 2.1, the retok fleet at HEAD, re-reads the pool. The tool is `tools/read_fleet_archive.sh` on `gpu_retok_out`, extended to print windows at the ceiling and slots freed per pass. This is a measurement at HEAD's live segmentation and decides nothing.

This is a reading of provenance, not a finding that the owner took none of them. So the owner is asked once, with no action needed. If you took any of them yourself, name it and it will stand as your ruling."

§8 0.2's [OWNER] clause is dropped, since that row is done (O20). The register's conditionals resolve to this reading, and the owner's answer can still revise them:
- 03b-16.23 / C14: the codec does not refresh at 04's redraw-only acts. `DATA_FOCUS_STAMP` 'opt' is the default, and 'all' is an arm.

- 03b-16.17: D-6's coordinate rows stay the default. The flip is read on BWT and stability-gap depth.

Safeguard.
- C14's narrowing of D-5 is the only departure from a D-item that rests on design reasoning rather than a GPU reading.
- 03b is unbuilt until S3. Before S3 builds the refresh rule, the manager re-reads the brief for an answer.
- If the owner has named D-5 by then, the narrowing is not built, and it goes back to the owner instead.

This ruling builds nothing and moves no default.
rulings.basis:
The owner's codec-era rulings are two, and both stand; no register ruling revises either:
- "no frozen codecs / nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary" (2026-09-25, `notes/AGENT_STATE.md:16-17`; `03b_LIVE_CODEC.md:52`);
- the approval of stream rebuilding (S0b, 2026-09-26, `notes/AGENT_STATE.md:47`).

The owner's "Otherwise things look pretty good" cannot be read as taking a D-item:
- it was said of Proposal 03, and recorded at 11:29 on 2026-09-25 (commit 12346bc);
- that was before the live-codec design's critic (eac5e59, 15:05) and before the D-items existed (7981378, 15:06).

Even if the owner took one, the risk is low and bounded:
- C14's narrowing leaves D-5's evident subject intact. D-5's "refreshed at each act" predates 04's redraw-only acts, and those acts do not move the text view.
- C44 and C45 keep D-4, D-7 and D-2 as the status quo until a GPU arm reads.
- The one departure that rests on design reasoning (C14) is unbuilt, and the safeguard holds it back.
So no register ruling overturns a D-item without a test behind it, and nothing irreversible happens before the owner can answer.

The draft's "The record answers it" and "were taken by the design and revision workflows" said more than the record does (checker A F12, checker B F20). The ruling now states only what the record shows, and names the reading as the manager's.

N3's own text makes these items revisable "unless the owner says they took one" (register l.139-141). The operating model delegates such details to the manager and names notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md as the owner's channel (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:112-140`).
